functions.name: ParseCharacterNameFromPacket
functions.comment:
Parses character name and ID from a network packet buffer.

Extracts a null-terminated character name (max 15 characters) from the packet
buffer pointed to by ESI, converts it from ANSI to Unicode, and stores it in
the global Unicode string buffer. Also extracts the character ID from the
packet and stores it in a global DWORD.

Algorithm:
1. Copy 16 bytes from packet buffer (ESI+1) to local stack buffer
2. Mask the last DWORD to ensure null termination (clear high byte)
3. Convert the ANSI string to Unicode using win2Unicode into g_adwData_6fbd4434
4. Extract character ID from ESI+0x11 and store in g_dwCharacterId

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT ESI - Pointer to packet data buffer containing:
    +0x01: char[15] - Character name (null-terminated ANSI string)
    +0x10: byte - Null terminator position
    +0x11: DWORD - Character ID

Returns:
  void - Results stored in globals:
    g_adwData_6fbd4434+4: Unicode character name
    g_dwCharacterId: Character unit ID

Packet Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size   Field              Type
  0x00    1      Packet opcode      byte
  0x01    15     Character name     char[15]
  0x10    1      (padding/null)     byte
  0x11    4      Character ID       DWORD

Special Cases:
  - Character name is truncated to 15 characters maximum
  - The & 0xFFFFFF mask clears byte at offset 0x0F ensuring null termination

functions.name: IsGameModeInPlayableState
functions.comment:
Validates whether game mode state allows active gameplay.

Algorithm:
1. Load current game mode state from g_dwGameModeState global variable
2. Test if state value equals 0x1 (Playing mode) - jump to return true if match
3. Test if state value equals 0x2 (Paused mode) - jump to return true if match
4. If neither condition met, clear EAX and return false (0x0)
5. If either condition met, set EAX to 0x1 and return true

Parameters:
(none) - Function uses global game mode state via g_dwGameModeState

Returns:
0x1 - Game is in playable state (state value is 1 or 2)
0x0 - Game is not in playable state (state value is any other value)

Special Cases:
Magic number 0x1: Game state representing active playing/gameplay mode
Magic number 0x2: Game state representing paused mode (gameplay suspended but game active)
Game logic requires active gameplay only when in these two specific states

functions.name: IsGameplayStateActive
functions.comment:
Checks if the game is in normal gameplay state (not in a menu or session UI).

Algorithm:
1. Read g_bInMenuSessionState global flag
2. Return TRUE if flag is 0 (gameplay active), FALSE if flag is 1 (in menu session)

Parameters:
  None (void)

Returns:
  bool - TRUE if gameplay is active (not in menu session state)
       - FALSE if currently in menu/session state

Global References:
  g_bInMenuSessionState (0x6fbcd5b0) - Set to 1 by FUN_6fac2530 when entering
    menu/UI session states, cleared to 0 by HandleGameSessionExit when exiting

Usage Context:
  This is a simple predicate function to query game UI state. The flag tracks
  whether the player is in certain UI modes (stash panel, trade session, etc.)
  versus normal gameplay.

functions.name: InitializeInventorySlotCounters
functions.comment:
Zero-initialize global inventory slot tracking counters

Algorithm:
1. Set g_dwCurrentInventoryTab to 0 (active tab selector)
2. Set g_dwInventorySlotCounter to 0 (slot iteration counter)
3. Return (no error conditions)

Parameters:
  (none)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  Called during main game initialization as part of UI subsystem setup
  Must be called before any inventory panel operations

functions.name: SendTradeExitPacket
functions.comment:
Sends a trade exit notification packet to the server.

Algorithm:
1. Set game mode state to 7 (trade exit mode)
2. Build a 7-byte packet structure on the stack:
   - Byte 0: 'O' (0x4F) - packet type identifier
   - Bytes 1-2: 0x0004 - sub-command or flags
   - Bytes 3-4: g_wPadValue - padding/session value
   - Bytes 5-6: g_dwCurrentError - current error code
3. Send the packet via SendChatMessageThrottled
4. Set trade exit state to -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) to indicate exit in progress

Parameters:
None - this function takes no parameters.

Returns:
void - no return value.

Called When:
- User clicks minimap home button while in active trade
- Both g_dwTradeGoldAmount and g_dwTradeAcceptState are non-zero

Packet Structure (7 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field           Value
0x00    1     bPacketType     'O' (0x4F)
0x02    2     wSubCommand     0x0004
0x04    2     wPadValue       from g_wPadValue
0x06    2     wErrorCode      from g_dwCurrentError

Side Effects:
- Sets g_dwGameModeState to 7
- Sets g_dwTradeExitState to 0xFFFFFFFF

functions.name: HandleSaveAndExitDialogConfirm
functions.comment:
Handles the "Save and Exit" dialog confirmation button callback.

Algorithm:
1. Stop any playing sounds by calling PlaySoundAtPosition with null parameters
2. Execute game end cleanup via ProcessGameEndCleanup()
3. Set game mode state to 3 (exiting/cleanup state)
4. Clear the save/exit dialog pointer (g_pSaveExitDialog = 0)
5. Build and send a "Save and Exit" network packet via SendChatMessageThrottled

Parameters:
- None (callback function takes no parameters)

Returns:
- 1 (TRUE): Always returns success

Network Packet Format:
| Offset | Value | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| 0      | 0x4F  | Packet type 'O' (Save and Exit command) |
| 1      | 0x03  | Sub-command: Save and Exit |
| 2-6    | 0x00  | Padding/Reserved |

Related Globals:
- g_dwGameModeState (0x6fbcd5ac): Game state machine, set to 3 on exit
- g_pSaveExitDialog (0x6fbcc994): Dialog window pointer, cleared on confirm

Called By:
- FUN_6fac2430: Dialog creation function that adds this as a button handler

functions.name: CreateGameExitDialog
functions.comment:
Creates and initializes the game exit confirmation dialog.

Algorithm:
1. Check if exit dialog already exists (g_pExitDialog != NULL)
2. If exists, trigger error with code 0x13d (dialog already open)
3. Create dialog window with dimensions 320x100 pixels
4. If creation fails, trigger error with code 0x529
5. Set dialog type flag at offset 0x5c to 1 (exit dialog type)
6. Add first text entry: difficulty string (via Ordinal_10004/GetDifficulty)
7. Add second text entry: exit button with InitiateGameExitSequence callback
8. Validate dialog entry count at offset 0x50 (must be < 0x80000000)
9. If validation fails, trigger error with code 0x4f2 or 0x4f8
10. Set selection index at offset 0x44 to -1 (no selection)

Parameters: None (void function)

Returns: void (exits via ReportError on failure paths)

Error Codes:
0x13d (317) - Dialog already exists
0x529 (1321) - Dialog creation failed  
0x4f2 (1266) - Dialog became NULL after text entries
0x4f8 (1272) - Entry count overflow

Magic Numbers:
0x140 (320) - Dialog width in pixels
0x64 (100) - Dialog height in pixels
0xFCB (4043) - String ID for difficulty text
0xD48 (3400) - String ID for exit button text
0x0F - Text color/style flag

Structure Layout (Dialog at g_pExitDialog):
Offset  Size  Field           Description
0x44    4     nSelectedIndex  Current selection (-1 = none)
0x50    4     nEntryCount     Number of text entries
0x5c    4     dwDialogType    Dialog type (1 = exit dialog)

Called By: FUN_6fac2530 (game state handler, case 0)

functions.name: CreateSaveExitDialog
functions.comment:
Creates the Save/Exit Game dialog with three text entry options.

Algorithm:
1. Check if dialog already exists (g_pSaveExitDialog != 0), return 0 if so
2. Call CreateDialogWindow(320, 100, ...) to create a 320x100 pixel dialog
3. Set dialog type flag at offset 0x5c to 1 (modal dialog)
4. Add three text queue entries via AddTextQueueEntry:
   a. Title text (string ID 0xFCA/4042) - no callback, index 0
   b. "Save and Exit" button (string ID 0xD49/3401) - HandleSaveAndExitDialogConfirm callback
   c. "Exit Game" button (string ID 0xD48/3400) - InitiateGameExitAlt callback
5. Validate dialog state and text entry count
6. Set dialog selection index at offset 0x44 to -1 (no selection)
7. Return 1 on success

Parameters:
- None (void)

Returns:
- 1 (TRUE): Dialog created successfully
- 0 (FALSE): Dialog already exists, or creation failed (aborts via ReportError)

String Resource IDs:
| ID     | Hex    | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| 4042   | 0xFCA  | Dialog title text |
| 3401   | 0xD49  | "Save and Exit" button |
| 3400   | 0xD48  | "Exit Game" button |

Dialog Structure Offsets:
| Offset | Size | Field | Description |
|--------|------|-------|-------------|
| 0x44   | 4    | dwSelectedIndex | Currently selected button (-1 = none) |
| 0x50   | 4    | dwTextEntryCount | Number of text entries in queue |
| 0x5c   | 4    | dwDialogType | Dialog type (1 = modal) |

Error Line Numbers:
- 0x529 (1321): CreateDialogWindow returned NULL
- 0x4F2 (1266): g_pSaveExitDialog became NULL after adding entries
- 0x4F8 (1272): Text entry count overflow (high bit set)

Related Globals:
- g_pSaveExitDialog (0x6fbcc994): Dialog window pointer

Called By:
- FUN_6fac2530: Game session packet handler (case 1)

functions.name: DispatchGameModePacket
functions.comment:
Dispatches game mode transition packets based on packet command type.

Algorithm:
1. Read packet command type from pPacketData[1], validate range 0x00-0x15
2. Save registers (EBX, EBP, ESI, EDI) and dispatch via jump table at 0x6fac2b80
3. Case 0x00 (0x6fac258c): Process game session initialization/cleanup
   - Check g_dwGameModeState, if non-zero jump to error handler
   - Verify g_bStashPanelOpen and call GetInitFlag
   - Loop through UI panels (g_adwUIPanelStates), check state and dispatch
   - Create exit dialog if conditions met, initialize trade session state
4. Case 0x01 (0x6fac2759): Process player inventory/exit request
   - Validate g_dwGameModeState == 0, check unit selection
   - Call CreateSaveExitDialog or send network packet 0x4F
   - Transition through UI panel states, set g_dwGameModeState = 2
5. Case 0x05 (0x6fac2947): Process trade cancellation
   - Exit if g_bStashPanelOpen == 0
   - Set g_dwTradeExitState = -1, call HandleGameSessionExit
   - Process trade state (g_dwTradeItemSlotCount, g_dwTradePanelState)
6. Case 0x06 (0x6fac2a35): Process trade completion confirmation
   - Send network packet 0x4F with position data
   - Dispatch based on g_dwGameModeState via secondary jump table
7. Case 0x09 (0x6fac26fd): Send player leave packet (type 0x17)
8. Case 0x0A (0x6fac2710): Process character ID lookup and validation
   - Hash g_dwCharacterId, traverse unit list, send packet
9. Cases 0x0C-0x0F: Various sound/audio processing calls
10. Case 0x10/0x11: Tail calls to FUN_6fb4c440/FUN_6fb4c870
11. Default (0x6fac2b7c): Invalid packet type, return immediately

Parameters:
- pPacketData: IMPLICIT in EAX - Pointer to network packet buffer
  [0]: Packet header/ID
  [1]: Command type (0x00-0x15)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Invalid command type (>0x15): Returns immediately without processing
- g_dwGameModeState != 0: Many cases jump to error handler at 0x6fac2b56
- g_pPlayerName != 0: Blocks certain state transitions

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x15: Maximum valid command type
- 0x26: Expected UI panel count for validation
- 0x4F: Network packet type for game state messages
- 0x17: Player leave game packet type
- 0x5A: Error code for invalid unit type

Jump Tables:
- Primary: 0x6fac2b80 (22 entries for cases 0x00-0x15)
- Secondary: 0x6fac2bd8 (5 entries for sub-dispatch in case 0x00)
- Secondary: 0x6fac2bec (5 entries for sub-dispatch in case 0x01)
- Secondary: 0x6fac2c00 (5 entries for sub-dispatch in case 0x05)
- Secondary: 0x6fac2c14 (7 entries for sub-dispatch in case 0x06)

Global State Modified:
- g_dwGameModeState: Game mode state machine value
- g_bStashPanelOpen: Stash panel visibility flag
- g_dwTradeExitState: Trade session exit state (-1 on cancel)
- g_dwTradeItemSlotCount: Trade slot counter
- g_dwTradePanelState: Trade panel state machine
- g_adwUIPanelStates: Array of UI panel state flags
- g_dwCharacterId: Current character unit ID

Error Handling:
- Jumps to OpenCharacterInventoryPacket at 0x6fac1fc0 on state errors
- Calls CleanupAndAbort/ReportError(-1) on fatal errors

functions.name: ProcessGameExitAndPanelCleanup
functions.comment:
Processes game exit and UI panel cleanup operations.

Handles multiple responsibilities based on game state:
1. Detects cursor position within specific UI panel regions and processes ordinal callbacks
2. Validates game context and room state for session exit
3. Closes stash panel and sends network close command (0x4F02)
4. Resets viewport, automap, cursor state, and sound entries on clean exit
5. Renders exit/save dialogs based on current game mode state

Algorithm:
1. Cache cursor position from global error state
2. If game mode > 2 and no active player:
   a. Check 3 UI panel hit regions (panel buttons)
   b. Call Ordinal_10004 and Ordinal_10137 for each hit
3. If game context exists:
   a. Get room from game context via UNITS_GetRoom
   b. Check unit type (0x11) for exit condition
   c. Process room via Ordinal_10691 and VectorPushElement
4. If stash panel open:
   a. Build close command packet "O\x02" (0x4F02)
   b. Send via SendChatMessageThrottled
   c. Validate UI panel count equals 0x26
   d. On clean exit: reset viewport, automap, cursor, sound
5. Handle exit dialogs for game modes 1-2

Parameters:
None (uses global state)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Returns early if stash panel not open and game context invalid
- Aborts with error if UI panel count != 0x26 (38 panels expected)
- Skips cleanup if ProcessGameExitTimeout returns non-zero

Magic Numbers:
- 0x111, 0x133: Panel X bounds (273-307 pixels)
- 0xdd, 0xff: Secondary panel X bounds (221-255 pixels)
- 0xa8, 0xca: Panel Y bounds region 1 (168-202 pixels)
- 0x17f, 0x1a1: Panel Y bounds region 2 (383-417 pixels)
- 0x26 (38): Expected UI panel count
- 0x11 (17): Unit type check for exit condition
- 0x1023, 0x1022: Ordinal call context IDs

Error Handling:
- If UI panel count validation fails, calls CleanupAndAbort with line 0x139B
- Fatal error terminates via ReportError(-1)

functions.name: CalculateDistanceSquared
functions.comment:
Calculate the squared Euclidean distance between two points on a 2D plane.

Algorithm:
1. Convert flDeltaX to float10 extended precision
2. Multiply flDeltaX by itself (flDeltaX²)
3. Convert flDeltaY to float10 extended precision
4. Multiply flDeltaY by itself (flDeltaY²)
5. Add the two squared values (flDeltaX² + flDeltaY²)
6. Return the sum as float10

Parameters:
- flDeltaX: X-axis delta distance (float)
- flDeltaY: Y-axis delta distance (float)

Returns:
- float10: Sum of squares (flDeltaX² + flDeltaY²), representing squared distance

Special Cases:
- Zero inputs: Returns 0.0
- Negative inputs: Squared values always positive
- Used for range/viewport checks where exact distance not needed

Related Functions:
- RenderGameViewport() - Uses distance for viewport clipping checks
- IsEffectInViewport() - Validates effect visibility based on squared distance
- InitializeGameObjectProperties() - Sets object position/collision calculations
- UpdateInventoryItemPosition() - Calculates item offset distances

functions.name: SetTimeout500Ms
functions.comment:
Sets a timeout deadline 500 milliseconds from current system time

Algorithm:
1. Get current system tick count from Windows API
2. Add 500 milliseconds (0x1f4 hex) to current time
3. Store calculated deadline in global timeout variable

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1f4 (500 decimal) - Timeout duration in milliseconds
0x6fbe8f14 - Global variable storing timeout deadline

Special Cases:
Timer wraps around after 49.7 days of system uptime due to DWORD overflow

functions.name: RenderScreenFadeOverlay
functions.comment:
Renders a screen fade overlay effect that fades out over 500 milliseconds

Algorithm:
1. Check if fade is active (g_dwFadeEndTime != 0)
2. Get current system tick count via GetTickCount
3. If current time exceeds fade deadline, clear timer and exit
4. Calculate viewport region based on split-screen mode:
   - Mode 0 (fullscreen): x=0, width=screen_width
   - Mode 1 (right viewport): x=0, width=screen_width/2
   - Mode 2 (left viewport): x=screen_width/2, width=screen_width
5. Calculate fade alpha: (remaining_time * 255) / 500
6. Call D2GFX.Ordinal_10016 to draw filled overlay rectangle

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x2f (47) - UI panel height offset subtracted from screen height
0xff (255) - Maximum alpha value for full opacity
500 (0x1f4) - Total fade duration in milliseconds

Global Variables:
g_dwFadeEndTime (0x6fbcd5a8) - Deadline timestamp when fade completes
g_dwViewportMode (0x6fbcd070) - Viewport mode (0=full, 1=right, 2=left)
g_dwScreenWidth (0x6fba7034) - Current screen width in pixels
g_dwScreenHeight (0x6fba7038) - Current screen height in pixels

External Calls:
GetTickCount - Windows API for system uptime in milliseconds
D2GFX.Ordinal_10016 - Draws filled rectangle with alpha transparency
  Parameters: (nX, nY, nWidth, nHeight, dwUnknown, nAlpha)

functions.comment:
Forwards a virtual method call through a wrapper object delegation pattern.

Algorithm:
1. Load inner object pointer from wrapper at offset 0x8
2. Retrieve vtable pointer from inner object
3. Tail-call virtual method at vtable offset 0x2c (index 11)

  0x00    4     vtable          void**    Wrapper vtable (unused here)
  0x08    4     pInnerObject    void*     Pointer to delegated object

Notes:
  - This is a thunk function implementing interface delegation
  - Part of a group of similar thunks (0x6fac3130, 0x6fac3140, etc.)
  - Each thunk forwards to a different vtable offset
  - Common pattern for COM-style or C++ wrapper classes

functions.name: CallVtableMethod9FromOffset8

  0x00    4     (wrapper)     Wrapper structure base
  0x08    4     pInnerObj     Pointer to inner object with vtable

Vtable Dispatch:

Notes:

  - No xrefs found - may be called via function pointer table

functions.name: CallSurfaceBltFast
functions.comment:
Thunk wrapper that calls IDirectDrawSurface::BltFast via vtable.

1. Dereference pGraphicsContext+0x8 to get IDirectDrawSurface interface pointer
2. Dereference interface pointer to get vtable
3. Tail-call virtual method at vtable offset 0x1C (BltFast method, index 7)

Parameters:
  pGraphicsContext (ECX): Pointer to graphics context structure containing
                          IDirectDrawSurface interface pointer at offset +0x8

Returns:

  Offset  Size  Field       Type                  Description
  0x00    0x08  (unknown)   byte[8]               Context data
  0x08    0x04  pSurface    IDirectDrawSurface*   DirectDraw surface interface

IDirectDrawSurface Vtable Reference:
  Offset 0x1C = BltFast() - Performs fast bit block transfer without clipping

BltFast Method:

  - Faster than Blt() but no stretch/rotate/clip support
  - Used for simple sprite/tile blitting operations

functions.name: HandleQueryEndSessionMessage
functions.comment:
Handles WM_QUERYENDSESSION Windows message for session termination.

Checks if a callback is registered at this+0x24 and invokes it when
receiving a WM_QUERYENDSESSION (0xD) message with specific flag conditions.
Used to allow the application to respond to system shutdown requests.

Algorithm:
  1. Check if callback pointer at this+0x24 is non-null
  2. Check if flag 0x40000000 is NOT set in nMsg+0xC (dwFlags)
  3. Check if message type at nMsg+0x8 equals 0xD (WM_QUERYENDSESSION)
  4. If all conditions met, call callback at this+0x28
  5. Return callback result or 0 if conditions not met

Parameters:
  this (ECX, IMPLICIT): Handler object containing callback pointers
    - Offset 0x24: Callback enabled flag (non-zero = enabled)
    - Offset 0x28: Function pointer to session end callback
  nMsg: Pointer to message structure
    - Offset 0x08: Message type (checked against 0xD)
    - Offset 0x0C: Message flags (checked for 0x40000000 bit)

Returns:
  Non-zero: Callback result (typically allows shutdown)
  0: Message not handled or conditions not met

Magic Numbers:
  0xD (13): WM_QUERYENDSESSION Windows message ID
  0x40000000: Flag indicating message should be ignored

functions.name: IsPointInBoundsAlt
functions.comment:
Tests if a point's coordinates fall within a rectangular bounds region.

Algorithm:
1. Extract point X coordinate from pPointData offset 0x0C (ushort)
2. Extract point Y coordinate from pPointData offset 0x0E (ushort)
3. Check X >= left boundary (in_EAX + 0x08)
4. Check X <= left + width (in_EAX + 0x08 + in_EAX + 0x1C)
5. Check Y >= bottom - height (in_EAX + 0x0C - in_EAX + 0x18)
6. Check Y <= bottom boundary (in_EAX + 0x0C)
7. Return TRUE (1) if all bounds checks pass, FALSE (0) otherwise

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT in_EAX - pBounds: Pointer to bounds structure with rectangle definition
  pBoundsInfo (ECX) - Unused in implementation, passed for API compatibility
  pPointData (EDX) - Pointer to structure with X (offset 0x0C) and Y (offset 0x0E) as ushorts

Returns:
  TRUE (1) - Point is within bounds (inclusive on all edges)
  FALSE (0) - Point is outside bounds

Structure Layout (pBounds via EAX):
  Offset  Size  Field      Type   Description
  0x08    4     nLeft      int    Left X boundary
  0x0C    4     nBottom    int    Bottom Y boundary
  0x18    4     nHeight    int    Height (subtracted from bottom for top)
  0x1C    4     nWidth     int    Width (added to left for right boundary)

Structure Layout (pPointData via EDX):
  Offset  Size  Field      Type    Description
  0x0C    2     wPosX      ushort  X coordinate of point
  0x0E    2     wPosY      ushort  Y coordinate of point

Note: Uses inclusive boundary checks (<= and >=), unlike IsPointInBounds 
which uses exclusive checks (< and >). This variant uses different
structure offsets (0x08/0x0C/0x18/0x1C vs 0x18/0x1C/0x24/0x28).

3. Extract mouse Y coordinate from pMouseEvent->wMouseY (ushort)

5. Test if Y is within vertical bounds [nBottomY - nHeight, nBottomY]
6. If within bounds: clear fEnabled flag, invoke pfnClickCallback
7. If outside bounds: clear both fState and fEnabled, return 0

Parameters:
  this (ECX)      - D2ControlClickRegion* - Pointer to UI control structure
  pMouseEvent     - D2MouseEvent* - Pointer to mouse event with coordinates

Returns:
  Callback return value if click is within bounds and control enabled
  0 if control is disabled or click is outside bounds

  Offset  Size  Field             Description
  0x08    4     nLeftX            Left edge X coordinate
  0x0C    4     nBottomY          Bottom edge Y coordinate  
  0x18    4     nHeight           Control height
  0x1C    4     nWidth            Control width
  0x20    4     fEnabled          Control enabled flag (0 = disabled)
  0x28    4     pfnClickCallback  Click handler callback function pointer
  0x2C    4     fState            Additional state flag

  0x0C    2     wMouseX           Mouse X coordinate (ushort)

functions.comment:

This function is part of the C++ destructor chain for StreamObject-derived classes.
It performs vtable unwinding by resetting the object's vtable pointer from the derived
class back to base class vtables, ensuring proper destructor chaining.

1. Set up Structured Exception Handler (SEH) frame for exception-safe destruction
2. Write intermediate vtable pointer (0x6fb88150) to object's vtable slot
3. Write final base class vtable (g_pVtbl_GameDataCollectionBase at 0x6fb843f8)
4. Tear down SEH frame by restoring previous exception handler chain
5. Return to caller (DestroyGameObject)

Parameters:
- pThis (GameDataCollectionBase*, Stack[0x4]): Pointer to the StreamObject instance being destroyed

Returns:
- void: No return value

Special Cases:
- Function is called as part of destructor chain from DestroyGameObject
- SEH frame protects against exceptions during vtable manipulation
- Two vtable writes occur: first intermediate (0x6fb88150), then base (0x6fb843f8)
- The intermediate vtable write may be for a middle class in inheritance hierarchy

- 0x6fb843f8: g_pVtbl_GameDataCollectionBase (base class vtable)
- 0x6fb7d91e: SEH exception filter/handler address

functions.name: ProcessTextInputKeypress
functions.comment:
Processes keyboard input for a text input field control.

Handles text editing operations including character insertion, deletion (backspace/delete),
cursor management, and input validation. Supports both regular text mode and numeric-only
input mode with maximum value enforcement.

Algorithm:
1. Check if input should be ignored based on focus state and key flags
2. For extended keys (> 0x7F), mark as processed and exit
3. Extract ASCII character from key event
4. Call character validation callback if registered
5. Handle special keys:
   - Backspace (0x08): Delete character before cursor, shift remaining left
   - Delete/Period (0x2E): Delete character at cursor position
   - Enter (0x0D) or Escape (0x1B): Call confirmation handler
   - Space/Enter/Escape with invalid char: Reject input
6. For valid characters: Insert at cursor, shift existing chars right
7. After insertion, validate text meets constraints (pixel width, numeric max)
8. If numeric mode, clamp value to maximum and update buffer

Parameters:
  this (IMPLICIT ECX) - Pointer to TextInput control structure
  pKeyEvent - Pointer to keyboard event data structure

Returns:
  1 - Input was processed (accepted or handled)
  0 - Input was rejected (unrecognized key in empty field)

  Offset  Size  Field                Description
  0x04    4     pfnCharValidator     Optional character validation callback
  0x18    4     dwUnknown18          Unknown field (passed to linked list lookup)
  0x1C    4     dwMaxPixelWidth      Maximum rendered text width in pixels
  0x20    4     fNumericOnly         Non-zero enables digit-only mode
  0x24    4     fIgnoreInput         Non-zero skips standard processing
  0x28    4     pwszTextBuffer       Pointer to Unicode text buffer (wchar_t*)
  0x30    4     dwMaxNumericValue    Maximum value for numeric mode

  0x42    4     pfnConfirmHandler    Callback for Enter/Escape handling

  0x1C    4     dwUnknown1C          Set to 0 after processing

Special Key Codes:
  0x08 - Backspace: Delete character before cursor
  0x0D - Enter: Confirm input
  0x1B - Escape: Cancel input
  0x2E - Period/Delete: Delete character at cursor

functions.name: AdvanceCharacterSelectSlot
functions.comment:
Advances the character selection slot position during character select screen animation.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if g_pGameContext is NULL (no active game context)
2. Calculate slot advancement based on current mode:
   - Mode 1 (Random): Use Linear Congruential Generator (LCG) with multiplier 0x6ac690c5
     to generate pseudo-random value, advance by 0x20 if (result & 0x3F) < 0x10
   - Other modes: Use data table lookup at g_adwData_6fba9a24[scrollPos * 7 + 6] for increment
3. Validate global state (DWORD_6fba9af4 must equal 7)
4. Validate scroll position is within bounds (< 7)
5. Check if slot position exceeds threshold (g_adwData_6fba9a24[scrollPos * 7 + 5] * 0x100)
6. If threshold exceeded:
   - Call FUN_6fac45b0() to check if looping is allowed
   - If looping: subtract GetPlayerClassScaledValue() to wrap position
   - If not looping: transition to next mode state
7. Handle mode transitions:
   - Mode 2 -> Mode 4, scroll position = 3, slot = 0
   - Mode 5 -> Mode 1, preserve scroll position, slot = 0

Parameters:
   None (uses globals)

Returns:
   void

Special Cases:
   - NULL game context: silent early return
   - Invalid DWORD_6fba9af4 (!= 7): calls error handler with line 0x9A (154)
   - Invalid scroll position (>= 7): calls error handler with line 0x9B (155)
   - Unhandled mode in transition: calls error handler with line 0x1E7 (487)

Magic Numbers Reference:
   0x6ac690c5 - LCG multiplier for pseudo-random number generation
   0x3F - Bit mask for extracting lower 6 bits of PRNG result
   0x10 - Threshold for PRNG advancement decision
   0x20 - Slot increment value in random mode
   0x100 (256) - Scale factor for threshold calculation (shift left 8)
   7 - Maximum number of character slots / validation constant

Global Variables Used:
   g_pGameContext (0x6fbcd050) - Game context pointer, contains PRNG state at +0x20, +0x24
   g_dwCharSelectMode (0x6fbcc98c) - Current character select mode (1-5)
   g_dwCharScrollPosition (0x6fbcc97c) - Current scroll position in character list
   g_dwSelectedCharSlot (0x6fbcc980) - Current selection slot position (animation progress)
   g_adwData_6fba9a24 - Character class data table (7 entries x 7 DWORDs each)
   DWORD_6fba9af4 - Validation constant (must be 7)

functions.name: ProcessHirelingPanelClick
functions.comment:
Processes mouse click events on the hireling panel UI.

Algorithm:
1. Load hireling panel context from global pointer
2. Check if hireling panel is open and click is within panel bounds:
   - Horizontal: (screenWidth/2 - 0x4A) to (screenWidth/2 + 0x47)
   - Vertical: (screenHeight - 0x45) to (screenHeight - 0x32)
3. If click is INSIDE bounds and panel context exists:
   - Check if panel is in active state (offset 0x10 == 1)
   - Return early based on state
4. If click is OUTSIDE bounds OR panel not open:
   - Mark event as handled (offset 0x18 = 1, offset 0x1C = 0)
   - Insert into cache via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie
   - If context is null, trigger fatal error (code 0x123)
   - If panel state != 1, iterate through handler list at offset 0xB08
   - If panel state == 1, check click timing via GetTickCount (debounce 0x50 ticks)
   - Find character slot at click position
   - Validate slot index against current selection and bounds
   - Execute slot callback from handler table (stride 0x110, base 0x170)
5. If callback returns 0 or validation fails, deactivate panel (state = 0)

Parameters:
pMouseEvent - Pointer to D2MouseEvent containing click coordinates
              wMouseX at offset 0x0C, wMouseY at offset 0x0E

Returns:
void - Modifies panel state and processes click handlers

Special Cases:
- Null panel context triggers fatal error via CleanupAndAbort
- Click debouncing prevents rapid repeated clicks (0x50 tick delay)
- Handler list traversal continues until handler returns 1

0x50      - Click debounce delay in ticks

0x170     - Handler table base offset in context
0xB08     - Handler linked list offset in context

functions.name: CleanupFadeEffectsAndDialogList
functions.comment:
Cleans up fade effects and processes the dialog context linked list during game session exit.

Algorithm:
1. Cache the dialog context list head pointer from g_pHirelingPanelContext
2. Check if fade effect is active (g_dwFadeEndTime != 0)
3. If active, process fade-out sound entries via ProcessSoundEntryArray with g_aFadeOutSoundEntries
4. Check if remote session features are supported via IsRemoteSessionSupported()
5. If remote session supported, process additional sound entries via g_aRemoteSessionSoundEntries
6. Decrement the fade effect reference counter (g_nFadeEffectRefCount)
7. Re-cache dialog list head (may have changed during sound processing)
8. Iterate through dialog context linked list:
   a. For each node, get next pointer at offset 0xB0C
   b. Call InitializeModule() to clean up current node
   c. Continue until list is exhausted (pNext == NULL)
9. Clear the dialog context list head to NULL

Parameters:
  None (uses global state)

Returns:
  void - No return value

  dwDialogListHead: Current node pointer during list traversal
  dwInitFlag: Result from GetInitFlag() indicating game state
  fRemoteSessionSupported: Boolean result from IsRemoteSessionSupported()
  pSoundEntryArray: Pointer to current sound entry array being processed
  extraout_var: PHANTOM - Compiler artifact for 32-bit bool return extension (ignore)

Special Cases:
  - If g_dwFadeEndTime is 0, skips all sound processing and counter decrement
  - Remote session sounds only processed if IsRemoteSessionSupported() returns true
  - Empty linked list (g_pHirelingPanelContext == 0) results in immediate list head clear

  0x6fba9940: g_aFadeOutSoundEntries - Sound entry array for fade-out effect (14 entries)
  0x6fba99e8: g_aRemoteSessionSoundEntries - Sound entry array for remote sessions (1 entry)
  0xB0C (2828): Offset to next pointer in dialog context structure
  0xE (14): Count of fade-out sound entries
  0x1 (1): Count of remote session sound entries

  0xB0C   0x4   pNext       dword*    Pointer to next node in linked list

functions.name: ProcessEscapeKeyMessage
functions.comment:
Processes an escape key message (type 0x1b) for the UI dialog system.

Algorithm:
1. Load g_dwLastError (dialog manager pointer)
2. If manager valid and within timeout window (tick < stored_time + 0x50):
   a. Mark message as complete (offset +0x18 = 1, +0x1c = 0)
   b. Insert message node into cache queue
   c. Return early (skip callback execution)
3. Otherwise, mark message complete and insert into cache
4. Assert dialog manager is valid (abort if null)
5. If callback counter > 4 and callback pointer at +0x60 is non-null:
   a. Execute the escape callback function
   b. Update timeout value for next operation

pMessageNode (void*) - Pointer to message node structure containing:
  +0x08: Message type (0x1b = escape key)
  +0x18: Completion status (set to 1 = processed)
  +0x1c: Result code (set to 0 = success)

- Asserts if g_dwLastError is null after cache insertion (fatal error)
- Callback at offset 0x60 only executed when counter > 4 (initialization complete)

0x1c2 (450) - Source line number for assertion

0x60 - Offset to escape callback function pointer

functions.comment:

When the user presses Enter (message type 0xD) in the hireling panel, this function

1. Extract wheel delta from mouse event structure at offset +0x0A
2. If delta is zero, skip navigation logic and mark event processed
3. Calculate scroll steps by dividing delta by 120 (WHEEL_DELTA constant)
4. Handle signed division rounding for negative values
5. If scroll steps are non-zero and hireling panel context exists:
   a. Iterate through linked list of scroll handlers at context+0xB08
   b. For each handler, call virtual function at vtable+0x08
   c. If any handler returns 1, exit early (event consumed)
6. If no handler consumed the event, call NavigateMenuSelection:
   - Direction -1 (scroll up/forward) for positive steps
   - Direction +1 (scroll down/backward) for negative steps
7. Mark event as processed: set flags at +0x18=1, +0x1C=0
8. Insert event into cache via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie

Parameters:
  pMouseEvent - Pointer to mouse event structure containing:
    +0x0A (short): nWheelDelta - Mouse wheel rotation delta
    +0x18 (dword): dwProcessedFlag - Set to 1 when handled
    +0x1C (dword): dwReserved - Set to 0 when handled

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - If g_pHirelingPanelContext is NULL, triggers fatal error (line 0x1F9)
  - Early return if any handler callback returns 1

Magic Numbers:
  0x78 (120) - Windows WHEEL_DELTA constant for one scroll notch
  0xB08 - Offset to handler linked list head in panel context
  0x1F9 (505) - Error line number for null context assertion

functions.name: ProcessHirelingPanelMouseMove
functions.comment:
Processes mouse movement events for the Hireling Panel UI.

Algorithm:
1. Validate g_pHirelingPanelContext is initialized (abort if null)
2. Check if within 80ms cooldown from last panel timestamp - if so, mark handled and return
3. Iterate through linked list of UI handlers at context+0xb08, calling each handler's vtable[3] method
4. If any handler returns 1, skip to marking message as handled
5. Set context+0x10 to 1 (processing flag) and update character slot hover state
6. If UpdateCharacterSlotHover returns non-zero, skip to marking message as handled
7. Extract cursor X,Y coordinates from message at offsets +0xc and +0xe
8. Check if cursor is within panel bounds (context+0x2c/0x30/0x34/0x38 define rectangle with 4px margin)
9. If outside bounds and hireling panel is open, check FUN_6fb71240
10. Call context+0x64 callback if set; if returns 0, exit without handling
11. If g_dwCursorStateFlag set, check IsCursorInQuickSkillButton - mark handled if inside
12. If g_bMinimapPartyButtonEnabled set, check IsCursorInMinimapPartyButton - mark handled if inside
13. If no callback at +0x64, call callback at +0x60 (required - aborts if null)

Parameters:
    pMouseMsg - Pointer to mouse message structure containing:
        +0x0c: wCursorX (ushort) - cursor X coordinate
        +0x0e: wCursorY (ushort) - cursor Y coordinate
        +0x18: dwHandled (dword) - set to 1 when message is processed
        +0x1c: dwResult (dword) - set to 0 when message is processed

Returns:
    void - Results communicated via pMouseMsg fields

Structure Layout (HirelingPanelContext at g_pHirelingPanelContext):
    Offset  Size  Field              Description
    0x00    4     dwLastTickCount    Last GetTickCount value for cooldown
    0x10    4     dwProcessingFlag   Set to 1 during mouse move processing
    0x2c    4     nPanelLeft         Panel left boundary X coordinate
    0x30    4     nPanelTop          Panel top boundary Y coordinate
    0x34    4     nPanelWidth        Panel width
    0x38    4     nPanelHeight       Panel height
    0x44    4     nHoveredSlot       Currently hovered character slot index
    0x48    4     nSelectedSlot      Currently selected character slot
    0x60    4     pfnDefaultHandler  Default mouse handler callback (required)
    0x64    4     pfnCustomHandler   Custom mouse handler callback (optional)
    0xb08   4     pHandlerList       Linked list of UI element handlers

Magic Numbers:
    0x50 (80)   - Cooldown period in milliseconds after panel timestamp
    0x15b (347) - Error code: null context at entry
    0x1aa (426) - Error code: null default handler callback
    4           - Pixel margin for bounds checking

functions.name: DispatchHirelingPanelInput
functions.comment:
Dispatches input events to hireling panel UI handlers.

Algorithm:
1. Check if 80ms (0x50) has elapsed since last input processing
2. If not enough time elapsed, skip processing (rate limiting)
3. Iterate through linked list of input handlers at context+0xB08
4. For each handler with valid object, call virtual method at vtable+0x14
5. If handler returns 1 (handled), mark event as processed and cache it
6. If no handler processes the input, update character slot hover state

Parameters:
  pInputEvent - Pointer to UIInputEvent structure containing event data

Returns:
  void - No return value. Side effects include:
    - pInputEvent->dwHandled set to 1 if handled
    - pInputEvent->dwReserved set to 0 if handled
    - Input cached via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie if handled
    - UpdateCharacterSlotHover called if not handled

UIInputEvent Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field          Description
  0x00    4     dwEventType    Type of input event
  0x04    4     dwEventData    Event-specific data
  0x08    4     nMouseX        Mouse X coordinate
  0x0C    4     nMouseY        Mouse Y coordinate  
  0x10    4     dwParam1       Additional parameter
  0x18    4     dwHandled      Set to 1 when event is processed
  0x1C    4     dwReserved     Set to 0 on successful dispatch

Handler Node Structure:
  Offset  Size  Field        Description
  0x00    4     pHandler     Pointer to handler object (has vtable)
  0x04    4     pNext        Pointer to next node in list

Handler Virtual Table:
  Offset  Size  Method       Description
  0x14    4     OnInput      Returns 1 if input was handled

Magic Numbers:
  0x50    80ms minimum delay between input processing
  0xB08   Offset to handler list head in hireling panel context
  0x14    Virtual table offset for OnInput method

functions.name: IsUnitTypeMonster
functions.comment:
Checks if a unit is of type Monster (dwType == 1).

Used as a callback filter function for unit enumeration routines like
Ordinal_10759 to find only Monster-type units in a room.

Algorithm:
1. Return FALSE if pUnit is NULL
2. Read dwType from offset 0x0 of UnitAny structure
3. Compare dwType against UNIT_TYPE_MONSTER (1)
4. Return TRUE if match, FALSE otherwise

Parameters:

Returns:

    1 = Monster

    3 = Missile

functions.name: IsUnitInVisibleRange
functions.comment:
Checks if a target unit is within the visible/selectable range of the source unit.

Algorithm:
1. Validate source unit (ESI) exists and is not locked (offset 0x10 == 0)
2. Get Act structure from source unit via Ordinal_10092 (GetActFromUnit)
3. Get coordinate bounds from game context (if exists), source unit, and target unit
   via Ordinal_11166 (GetUnitCoordinateBounds)
4. Compare coordinate ranges based on Act type:
   - Act 1 (0x13c == 1): Uses alternate coordinate comparison order
   - Other Acts: Uses standard X coordinate range comparison
5. Return TRUE (1) if target is in valid range, FALSE (0) otherwise

Parameters:
  pTargetUnit - Pointer to the target unit to check visibility against
  IMPLICIT ESI (unaff_ESI) - Pointer to the source unit performing the visibility check

Returns:
  1 (TRUE) - Target unit is within visible/selectable range
  0 (FALSE) - Target unit is not visible (source invalid, locked, or out of range)

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 immediately if source unit is NULL
  - Returns 0 immediately if source unit is locked (offset 0x10 != 0)
  - Uses zero coordinates if game context is NULL

Ordinal Calls:
  Ordinal_10092 - GetActFromUnit: Returns Act pointer containing level info
  Ordinal_11166 - GetUnitCoordinateBounds: Fills X min/max coordinate pair

Structure Layout (Unit):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x10    4     dwLockState     Non-zero indicates unit is locked/busy

Structure Layout (Act):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x13c   1     bActType        Act identifier (1 = Act 1, other = Acts 2-5)

functions.name: AdjustCoordinatesForViewportSplit
functions.comment:
Adjusts screen coordinates for split-screen viewport rendering.

When split-screen mode is active (Ordinal_10037 returns non-zero), applies a
perspective interpolation formula that scales coordinates based on their distance
from the screen center. This creates a parallax-like effect for unit positioning.

Algorithm:
1. Check if split-screen viewport mode is active via Ordinal_10037
2. If active:
   a. Apply decay factor (39/40) to Y coordinate: Y = Y - Y/40
   b. Calculate perspective scale: scale = 40 - (Y / 4)
   c. Apply X interpolation: X = X + scale * (X - screenWidth/2) / (screenWidth/2)
3. Apply final viewport offsets to both coordinates:
   - X += g_nViewportCenterOffsetX - g_dwViewportOffsetX
   - Y += g_nViewportCenterOffsetY - 8

Parameters:
  pnScreenX - Pointer to X screen coordinate (modified in place)
  IMPLICIT EBX - Pointer to Y screen coordinate (modified in place)

Returns:
  void - Coordinates modified through pointers

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x28 (40) - Full perspective scale factor
  0x66666667 - Magic constant for divide-by-40 optimization (signed)
  0x4 - Y coordinate division factor for perspective
  0x8 - Fixed Y offset adjustment constant

Special Cases:
  - If split mode inactive, only viewport offsets applied (no perspective)
  - Uses implicit EBX register as second coordinate pointer

functions.name: AdjustPositionToValidRoomCoords
functions.comment:
Adjusts a position to valid room coordinates using the player's current room.

Algorithm:
1. If unit (EDI) is NULL, use input coordinates from pnOutX and EBX
2. If unit exists, extract X/Y from unit based on unit type:
   - Types 2, 4, 5: Read coords directly from path data structure (offset 0xC=X, 0x10=Y)
   - Other types: Call Ordinal_10465 (GetPathX) and Ordinal_10030 (GetPathY)
3. Get the player's current room from g_pGameContext via UNITS_GetRoom
4. Validate position is within room using Ordinal_10561 (IsPositionInRoom)
5. Find nearest valid tile via Ordinal_10470 (FindNearestWalkableTile)
6. If valid position found, update output coordinates and return NULL
7. On failure, return original unit pointer

Parameters:
  pnOutX - Pointer to X coordinate (input/output)
  IMPLICIT EBX - Pointer to Y coordinate (input/output)
  IMPLICIT EDI - Unit pointer (NULL to use input coords)

Returns:
  NULL (0) - Success, coordinates adjusted in output parameters
  EDI - Failure, returns original unit pointer

Unit Type Classification (offset 0x00):
  2 = Missile
  4 = Item
  5 = Tile

Path Data Structure (offset 0x2C):
  +0x0C = nPosX (current X coordinate)
  +0x10 = nPosY (current Y coordinate)

functions.name: ValidateUnitClickThrottle
functions.signature: int ValidateUnitClickThrottle(int nYCoord, int nParam2, int nXCoord2, int nYCoord2)
functions.comment:
Validates unit click action and enforces 500ms throttle cooldown.

This function is called during unit selection to determine if a click
on a unit should be processed or throttled. It performs bounds checking,
validates the unit type, and manages a time-based cooldown system.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer (ESI) is non-null
2. Check unit type equals 5 (tile/object type)
3. Call IsPointWithinUnitBounds with first coordinate pair (ECX, nYCoord)
4. Call IsPointWithinUnitBounds with second coordinate pair (nXCoord2, nYCoord2)
5. Call Ordinal_10775 to validate selection context with nParam2
6. Check g_fTargetingEnabled global is non-zero
7. Compare g_dwCurrentGameTick against g_dwNextClickAllowedTick
8. If tick < next allowed: cooldown expired, add 500ms, return TRUE
9. If tick >= next allowed and EDI flag is 0: set flag to 1, return FALSE
10. Otherwise return FALSE (still in cooldown period)

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT ESI - pUnit: Pointer to unit being clicked (must be type 5)
  IMPLICIT ECX - nXCoord: X coordinate for first bounds check
  IMPLICIT EDI - pfThrottleTriggered: Output flag, set to 1 on first throttle
  nYCoord: Y coordinate for first bounds check
  nParam2: Validation parameter passed to Ordinal_10775
  nXCoord2: X coordinate for second bounds check
  nYCoord2: Y coordinate for second bounds check

Returns:
  1 (TRUE) - Click action is allowed (cooldown expired)
  0 (FALSE) - Click action is throttled or validation failed

Magic Numbers:
  0x5 - Unit type constant for tiles/objects
  0x1f4 (500) - Throttle cooldown period in milliseconds

Globals Referenced:
  g_fTargetingEnabled (0x6fbcd224) - Targeting system enable flag
  g_dwCurrentGameTick (0x6fbb874c) - Current game time in ms
  g_dwNextClickAllowedTick (0x6fbb8788) - Next allowed click timestamp

functions.name: FindNearbyMonsterTarget
functions.comment:
Searches adjacent tiles in 8 directions to find a valid monster target.

Algorithm:
1. Get unit facing direction via Ordinal_11172
2. Get unit's current room via UNITS_GetRoom
3. Iterate through 8 directional offsets from g_adwDirectionIndexTable
4. For each direction:
   a. Calculate direction index = (table_value + (facing >> 3)) & 7
   b. Get unit X coordinate (from path offset 0xC or Ordinal_10465)
   c. Get unit Y coordinate (from path offset 0x10 or Ordinal_10030)
   d. Apply X/Y offsets from direction tables (g_anDirectionXOffsets, g_anDirectionYOffsets)
   e. Check if position is valid in room via Ordinal_10152 (flags 0x180)
   f. Search for monster at position via Ordinal_10759 with IsUnitTypeMonster callback
   g. Validate target has targeting flag bit 2 set at offset 0xC4
   h. Check skill compatibility via GetSkillDescriptionFlags and CompareUnitTargetValidity
5. If valid target found, call Ordinal_10129 to set target and return monster
6. If all 8 directions checked with no valid target, return NULL

Parameters:
    nSkillRecord - Skill record index for target validation checks
    IMPLICIT pUnit (EBX) - Source unit to search around

Returns:
    UnitAny* - Pointer to found monster unit, or NULL if no valid target

Magic Numbers:
    0x180 - Room position validation flags
    0xC4 - Offset to unit flags dword, bit 2 = targetable
    0xC/0x10 - Path structure X/Y coordinate offsets
    6 - Skill flag index for GetSkillDescriptionFlags check

Unit Type Enumeration:
    2 = Object, 3 = Missile, 4 = Item, 5 = Tile (use path struct directly)
    Others = Use Ordinal_10465/Ordinal_10030 for coordinates

Ordinal References:
    Ordinal_11172 - D2Common.GetUnitDirection (facing)
    Ordinal_10465 - D2Common.GetPathX
    Ordinal_10030 - D2Common.GetPathY
    Ordinal_10152 - D2Common.CheckRoomCoords (validity)
    Ordinal_10759 - D2Common.FindUnitInRoom (with filter callback)
    Ordinal_10129 - D2Common.SetUnitTarget

functions.name: FindNearestSelectableUnit
functions.signature: UnitAny * FindNearestSelectableUnit(dword dwSelectFlags, UnitAny * pUnit, int * pnOutX, int * pnOutY)
functions.comment:
Finds the nearest selectable unit at or near the given coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. If input pUnit is NULL, skip to unit search
2. Check if unit has special selection flags (0x10000 in flags field)
3. For player units (type 0), return early if mode is 0 or 0x11 (idle/special)
4. For monster units (type 1), return early if mode is 0 or 0xC
5. Extract X/Y coordinates from the unit's path data based on unit type:
   - Types 2,4,5: Read directly from path structure offsets 0xC/0x10
   - Other types: Call Ordinal_10465/10030 (D2Common.GetPathX/GetPathY)
6. Determine search flags based on bit mask check (0x2003 or 0x300F)
7. If selection mode 0x5A (item mode): use IsItemUnitValid filter, flags=0x20
8. Initialize search parameter array (14 DWORDs, cleared to zero)
9. Get room from player context, enumerate nearby units via Ordinal_10101
10. Iterate found units, compute distance via Ordinal_10622
11. Validate each unit with ValidateUnitClickPosition
12. Track closest valid unit (minimum distance, starting threshold 0xA)
13. Free search allocation and return best match

Parameters:
  dwSelectFlags - IMPLICIT in_EAX: Selection context/mode flags
  pUnit - Initial unit to validate/extract coords from (may be NULL)
  pnOutX - Output pointer for X coordinate
  pnOutY - Output pointer for Y coordinate

Returns:
  UnitAny* - Nearest valid selectable unit, or NULL if none found

Special Cases:
  - Returns input pUnit early if it passes initial validation checks
  - Returns pUnit if it's a valid item (type 4) in item selection mode
  - Returns NULL (via pUVar9 init) if no units found or all fail validation

Magic Numbers:
  0x10000 - Unit flag indicating special/unselectable state
  0x11 - Player idle mode (return early)
  0xC - Monster special mode (return early)  
  0x5A - Item selection mode return from Ordinal_11151
  0x2003, 0x300F - Search flag combinations
  0x20 - Item-only search flags
  9 - Search radius parameter
  0xA - Initial distance threshold (10 units)

functions.name: ResolveSkillTargetUnit
functions.signature: UnitAny * ResolveSkillTargetUnit(dword dwSelectFlags, int * pnOutX, int * pnOutY, byte bInputFlags, int nAllowMonsterSearch)
functions.comment:
Resolves the target unit for a skill action, validating the unit and extracting coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Get current skill record via Ordinal_10733
2. If input unit (in_EAX) exists:
   a. For player units (type 0), check state flags - return early if unit is in invalid state
   b. Check skill mask flags against unit - skip if masked out
   c. Validate unit is selectable type via IsUnitSelectableType
   d. Handle automap target tracking and viewport state updates
   e. Extract X/Y coordinates from unit via GetUnitXCoord/GetUnitYCoord
3. Compare target coords against player position - if same, apply directional offset
4. Check input flags for special handling conditions
5. Based on skill targeting flags, delegate to specialized target finders:
   - FindNearestSelectableUnit: Search for nearby selectable units
   - FindNearbyMonsterTarget: Search for monster targets (if nAllowMonsterSearch set)
   - AdjustPositionToValidRoomCoords: Snap position to valid room coordinates

Parameters:
  dwSelectFlags - Selection flags passed to sub-target-finders
  pnOutX - Output pointer for target X coordinate
  pnOutY - Output pointer for target Y coordinate
  bInputFlags - Input flags controlling search behavior:
    0x01 = Allow position adjustment
    0x08 = Enable extended search
    0x20 = Disable fallback search
  nAllowMonsterSearch - If non-zero, allows FindNearbyMonsterTarget fallback
  IMPLICIT in_EAX - Input unit to validate/extract coords from (may be NULL)

Returns:
  UnitAny* - Resolved target unit, or NULL if coords-only result

Skill Record Offsets:
  +0x05 = Skill use mask (checked in caller)
  +0x06 = Target type flags (bit flags for search delegation)
  +0x07 = Unit validation mask

Unit State Flags (offset 0xC4):
  0x10000 = Unit in special state (early return)

Unit Type Values:
  0 = Player
  1 = Monster  
  2 = Missile
  4 = Item
  5 = Tile

Global Dependencies:
  g_pGameContext @ 0x6fbcd050 - Player unit context
  g_dwFadeEndTime @ 0x6fbcd57c - Fade transition state
  g_bUnitSelected @ 0x6fbcd578 - Unit selection state
  g_pPlayerName @ 0x6fbb1a58 - Player name pointer
  gdwBitMasks_exref @ 0x6fb7fe34 - Skill/unit bit masks

functions.name: ProcessCursorInputForViewport
functions.comment:
Processes cursor input and routes to appropriate viewport or selection handler.

This function serves as the primary cursor input dispatcher for the game viewport.
It determines whether cursor clicks should trigger unit selection or viewport
coordinate adjustments based on current viewport mode and cursor position.

Algorithm:
1. If viewport mode is not 3 (full-screen automap):
   a. Copy cursor position (g_nCursorPosX/Y) to output parameters
   b. Check if cursor Y is below bottom status bar (screen height - 0x31)
   c. If cursor is within text queue bounds and text queue is active, process unit selection
   d. Otherwise, check viewport split mode:
      - Mode 1: If cursor X < screen center, adjust for split viewport
      - Mode 2: If cursor X >= screen center, adjust for split viewport
      - Other modes: Always adjust for viewport split
2. If viewport mode is 3 or cursor below status bar:
   a. If no fade in progress (g_dwFadeEndTime == 0):
      - Check for automap target unit
      - Clear unit selection state
      - If previous selection was type 5 (tile), update viewport state

Parameters:
  pnCursorX - Pointer to receive/store cursor X coordinate (ECX)
  IMPLICIT EAX - Pointer to receive/store cursor Y coordinate

Returns:
  0 - Viewport coordinates were adjusted (AdjustCoordinatesForViewportSplit called)
  1 - Unit selection was processed or cursor was in status bar region

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x31 (49) - Height of bottom status bar in pixels
  0x3 - Full-screen automap viewport mode
  0x1 - Left split viewport mode
  0x2 - Right split viewport mode
  0x5 - Tile unit type constant

Special Cases:
  - Text queue bounds checked only when g_bTextQueueActive is set
  - Automap target finding only occurs when g_pAutomapTargetUnit is set
  - Tile selection (type 5) triggers room update via Ordinal_10310

functions.name: FindBestSelectableUnit
functions.comment:
Finds the best selectable unit under or near the cursor position.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if screen fade is in progress (g_dwFadeEndTime != 0)
2. Initialize click flags via FUN_6fac7510 (mouse/keyboard input state)
3. Check if current selected unit is still valid and selectable
4. If not, iterate through all units in visible rooms to find best target
5. For each room, traverse the unit linked list (offset 0x74 from room tile)
6. Apply priority-based selection using unit type weights from g_abData_6fba9924
7. Skip items (type 3), missiles (type 4 when DWORD_6fbcd574 set), and player's own unit
8. Compare candidates by priority weight, then by distance if equal priority
9. Process final selection with ProcessUnitSelection()

Parameters:
  None (uses global game context)

Returns:
  void - Updates selection state via ProcessUnitSelection()

Unit Type Constants:
  0 = Player
  1 = Monster (NPC)
  2 = Object (shrines, chests, portals)
  3 = Item (skipped - not selectable via this path)
  4 = Missile (conditionally skipped)

Priority Weights (from g_abData_6fba9924):
  - Lower value = higher selection priority
  - Players with selectable flag get priority boost (weight=1)
  - Monsters marked hostile get priority boost (weight=-8)

Safety:
  - Infinite loop protection at 30000 iterations
  - Validates click position and throttle before selection

Special Cases:
  - Object type (2) has special visibility checks via Ordinal_10789
  - Uses IsUnitBetweenCameraAndTarget for occlusion detection

functions.name: IsTargetingEnabled

Check if targeting mode is currently active

functions.name: CheckTimeoutElapsed50ms
functions.comment:
Checks if 50 milliseconds have elapsed since the last timeout check.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current tick count via GetTickCount()
2. Calculate elapsed time as (current_tick - g_dwLastTimeoutCheck)
3. If elapsed time >= 0x32 (50ms):
   - Update g_dwLastTimeoutCheck to current tick count
   - Return 1 (true - timeout elapsed)
4. Otherwise return 0 (false - timeout not yet elapsed)

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
1 (true) - 50ms or more have elapsed since last check
0 (false) - Less than 50ms have elapsed

Special Cases:
- Initial call when g_dwLastTimeoutCheck is 0 will likely return 1
- Used for frame-rate throttling in rendering loops

Magic Numbers:
0x32 = 50 decimal (millisecond threshold)

Related Functions:
- RenderPanelUI() - Calls this function for render throttling
- GetTickCount() - System API for millisecond timestamp

functions.name: SetLastError
functions.comment:

9. If expansion enabled, render additional expansion-specific death text

Parameters:

Returns:

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if g_pGameContext is NULL
  - Sets g_dwPad_6fbcd38c to 0 on invalid unit type/state
  - Caches loaded archive files in DWORD_6fbcd390 and DWORD_6fbcd394

functions.name: LoadAutomapActResources
functions.comment:
Loads automap UI resources based on the current act level.

Algorithm:
1. Check if game context and player room are valid
2. If not valid, cleanup existing automap archive handle and return
3. Get level number from current room via Ordinal_10691
4. If level number changed from cached value:
   a. Initialize palette colors (green=0x80, yellow=0xC0, red=0xFF)
   b. Cleanup existing archive handle
   c. Reset load progress counter
5. If load progress < 0x78 (120 frames):
   a. Increment load progress
   b. Get level data string offset via Ordinal_10142
   c. Determine act folder: "ACT%d" for levels < 0x6D, "EXPANSION" otherwise
   d. Get locale via Ordinal_10008
   e. Build resource path: "DATA\LOCAL\{locale}\UI\{act}\{level}"
   f. Check for special quest-based UI overrides (loops through quest table)
   g. If no archive loaded, load via LoadArchiveFileBySelector
   h. Position UI via Ordinal_10172 at (screenHeight/2 - 140)
6. If load progress >= 0x78 and archive exists, cleanup and return

Parameters:
  None (uses global game context)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Level >= 0x6D (109): Uses "EXPANSION" folder instead of ACT folders
  - Quest system inactive (g_fQuestSystemInitialized == 0): Aborts with error 0x60
  - Quest index > 0x24 (36): Aborts with error 0x65
  - Quest entries may override path to ACT1 folder for special UI

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x78 (120): Maximum load progress frames
  0x6D (109): First expansion level number
  0x145 (325): String table offset for level names
  0x8C (140): Y-offset for automap UI positioning
  0xD (13): Quest table entry size (stride)

functions.name: LoadUIArchiveFile
functions.comment:
LoadUIArchiveFile - Load UI asset file from MPQ archive

Algorithm:
1. Format full path using wsprintf with base path and filename
2. Calculate string length via CalculateStringLength
3. If path is non-empty, strip to base filename:
   - Walk path backwards to find last path separator
   - Extract filename portion only
4. Call LoadArchiveFileBySelector to load from appropriate MPQ

Parameters:
  (via unaff_ESI): Pointer to filename string (char*)

Returns:
  undefined (loads archive file into memory)

Called By:
  52 locations during UI initialization including:
  - InitializeUISubsystem, InitializeAllUiAssetHandles
  - RenderStashPanelBackground, RenderSkillIconWithTooltip
  - LoadSkillTreeUIArchive, LoadHirelingPortrait

Notes:
- Uses 0x104 (260) byte stack buffer for path formatting
- Path separator stripping handles both '/' and '\\' separators
- Delegates to LoadArchiveFileBySelector for expansion pack handling

functions.name: CheckCursorPositionChanged
functions.comment:
CheckCursorPositionChanged - Processes UI state changes and cleanup

Algorithm:
1. If g_dwTargetFlags set:
   a. Request minimap state change
   b. If minimap not visible, make visible and hide party panel
   c. Process sound entries at 0x6fba6d2c
   d. Clear target flags
2. Process g_dwTargetCursorY virtual call at vtable+0x2C
3. If g_pPlayerName set, run game end cleanup
4. Cleanup virtual objects via vtable[0](1) calls:
   - g_dwTargetCursorX, g_dwTargetCursorY
   - g_dwTargetPrevCursorX, g_dwTargetPrevCursorY
5. Handle dialog mode transitions:
   - Mode 0: Clear padding array
   - Mode 1-4: Reset inventory slot, transition game mode 0xD->0xC

Parameters:
- None (uses global state)

Returns:
- void

Globals Modified:
- g_dwMinimapRequestedState, g_dwMinimapVisibleState
- g_dwPartyPanelVisibleState, g_dwTargetFlags
- g_dwStatAllocationValue, g_pPlayerName
- g_dwTargetCursorX/Y, g_dwTargetPrevCursorX/Y
- g_dwInventoryCurrentSlot, g_dwGameModeState

functions.name: RenderDialogControlValue
functions.comment:
Renders a dialog control's numeric value as formatted text.

Algorithm:
1. Validate g_dwLastError has bit 1 set (debug/render mode enabled)
2. Validate g_pGameContext is non-null
3. Find dialog control by ID in active dialog list
4. If found, extract value at control+0x18
5. Initialize Unicode buffer (12 wide chars) via constructor loop
6. Format value as ANSI string using "%d" format
7. Convert ANSI to Unicode via win2Unicode
8. Render text at position (25, 4) with line height 0

Parameters:
  dwControlId (ECX) - Dialog control identifier to look up

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if debug bit not set in g_dwLastError
  - Returns early if g_pGameContext is null
  - Returns early if dialog control not found

Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field         Type    Description
  0x00    4     pDialog       ptr     Dialog pointer from FindDialogByControlId
  0x18    4     dwValue       dword   Numeric value to render

Magic Numbers:
  0x02 - Debug/render mode bit mask in g_dwLastError
  0x0C - Count of Unicode characters in buffer (12)
  0x19 - X position for text rendering (25)
  0x04 - Y position for text rendering (4)
  0x258 - Line height parameter (600)

Cancel button click handler for dialog UI.

Ordinal 220 (0x10fa0)

functions.name: HandleStatAllocationConfirm
functions.comment:
Handles the OK/Confirm button click in the stat allocation dialog.

Algorithm:
1. Call CheckCursorPositionChanged to update cursor state
2. If no stat points allocated (g_dwStatAllocationValue == 0):
   a. If dialog mode is not 2 (party), return immediately
   b. Otherwise send game state packet and return
3. Based on dialog mode, send appropriate network packet:
   - Mode 0/1: Send chat message with allocated value (gold/trade)
   - Mode 2: Send game state packet + play sound
   - Mode 3: Send short packet type 0x14 (stat allocation)
   - Mode 4: Send short packet type 0x13 (skill allocation)
4. Play confirmation sound for modes 2-4
5. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
   None (callback function)

Returns:
   1 - Always returns success

Magic Numbers Reference:
   0x14 (20) - Network packet type for stat point allocation
   0x13 (19) - Network packet type for skill point allocation
   0xFFFFFFFF - Invalid/null entity ID for chat message
   0x0C - Offset to entity ID in game context

Dialog Modes:
   0 - Gold transfer mode
   1 - Trade mode
   2 - Party/game state mode
   3 - Stat point allocation mode
   4 - Skill point allocation mode

functions.name: HandleLevelUpDialogClose
functions.comment:
Callback handler invoked when the level-up stat allocation dialog is closed.

  - InitializeLevelUpDialog: Creates the dialog and registers this callback
  - CreateDialogWindowWithBackground: Dialog creation function that accepts this callback

functions.name: BuildMonsterAffixText
functions.comment:
Builds monster affix text for Champion/Unique monsters in the UI tooltip.

Algorithm:
1. Check if viewport mode is not split-screen (mode != 3)
2. Verify no target unit is currently selected (g_dwTargetUnitId == 0)
3. Clear the monster affix buffer (g_wszMonsterAffixBuffer = 0)
4. Validate unit pointer is not null
5. Check if unit is a Monster type (dwType == 1)
6. Check if monster has Champion flag (pMonsterData+0x16 & 0x08) or
   Unique/SuperUnique flag (pMonsterData+0x16 & 0x10)
7. If special monster, call FUN_6fad3c90 to build affix string into buffer

Parameters:
  pUnit (ECX): Pointer to unit structure (UnitAny*). Must be a monster (dwType == 1)
               with valid pMonsterData at offset 0x14.

Returns:
  1 (TRUE) - Monster affix text was successfully built into g_wszMonsterAffixBuffer
  0 (FALSE) - No affix text built (not a champion/unique, or preconditions failed)

Special Cases:
  - Returns 0 if viewport is in split-screen mode (mode == 3)
  - Returns 0 if another unit is currently targeted
  - Returns 0 if pUnit is NULL or not a monster type

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x03 - Split-screen viewport mode
  0x01 - Monster unit type (dwType)
  0x08 - Champion monster flag (in pMonsterData+0x16)
  0x10 - Unique/SuperUnique monster flag (in pMonsterData+0x16)
  0x14 - Offset to pMonsterData pointer in unit structure
  0x16 - Offset to monster type flags in MonsterData structure
  0x100 - Buffer size for affix string (256 wide chars)

Structure Layout (Unit offsets used):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
  0x00    4     dwType          uint    Unit type (1 = Monster)
  0x14    4     pMonsterData    ptr     Pointer to MonsterData structure

Structure Layout (MonsterData offsets used):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
  0x16    1     bMonsterFlags   byte    Monster type flags (Champion/Unique)

functions.name: GetRosterUnitControlText
functions.signature: int GetRosterUnitControlText(void * this, void * pUnit, Unicode * pTextBuffer, int * pnPercentValue)
functions.comment:
Retrieves the display text and percentage value for a roster unit's dialog control.

Searches the roster list for a matching unit by GUID, then finds the associated
dialog control and extracts its text label and current value as a percentage.

Algorithm:
1. Extract unit GUID from pUnit+0xC (or -1 if null)
2. Search g_pRosterList linked list for matching GUID at offset 0x8
3. Get control ID from roster entry at offset 0xC
4. Validate unit type (offset 0x10 must be non-zero and not 0xC)
5. Find dialog control via FindDialogByControlId
6. Copy control text (offset 0x66) to Unicode buffer
7. Get control value and calculate percentage: (value * 128) / 100
8. Compare dialog states via CompareDialogControlStates
9. Set output flag via EDI if states differ

Parameters:
  pUnit (ECX) - Unit structure pointer, GUID at offset 0xC, type at 0x10
  pTextBuffer - Output Unicode buffer for control text (128 chars max)
  pnPercentValue - Output pointer for calculated percentage value
  IMPLICIT: EDI points to state change flag output (set to 1 if changed)

Returns:
  1 - Success, text and percentage retrieved
  0 - Failure (null unit, roster entry not found, or control not found)

Structure Layout - Roster Entry:
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  0x08    4     dwUnitGUID    Unit identifier for lookup
  0x0C    4     nControlId    Associated dialog control ID
  0x30    4     pNext         Next entry in linked list

Structure Layout - Dialog Control:
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  0x66    var   szText        Control display text (ANSI)

Magic Numbers:
  0xC (12)  - Excluded unit type (possibly NPC or special unit)
  0x80 (128) - Maximum text buffer size
  100       - Percentage divisor for value calculation

functions.name: BuildUnitTooltipDisplay
functions.comment:
Builds and displays the tooltip information for a unit (monster/NPC) in the game UI.

Algorithm:
1. Save current floating-point precision via Ordinal_10047
2. Validate unit pointer and retrieve monster class ID from unit[1]
3. Calculate pointer to MonStats record: MonStats[nMonsterClassId * 0x1a8]
4. Initialize 0x800-element Unicode buffer for tooltip text
5. Check MonStats flags to determine display mode (bit masks at offsets 0x4 and 0x1c)
6. If displayable unit with valid skillstring (offset 0x6 != 0):
   a. Adjust vertical position by subtracting skill byte from g_dwUnitNameCacheIndex
   b. Build tooltip string: prefix + name + suffix using Unicode strcat
   c. If unit is type 0xC (portal), check room/level validity
   d. Calculate health bar value and determine color mode (0=normal, 1=portal, 3=champion, 4=boss)
   e. Check for special monster IDs (243, 333, 211, etc.) to force boss color
   f. Call CalculateViewportSplitRegions and render if valid
   g. Check immunity flags and build stat summary string
7. If not displayable, clear WORD_6fbd3f80 and show simple name if no target
8. Restore floating-point precision

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to UnitAny structure (can be NULL, handled gracefully)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - NULL pUnit: Sets nMonsterClassId to -1, skips processing
  - Portal units (type 0xC): Additional room validation, shows level name in parentheses
  - Boss monsters: IDs 0xF3, 0x14D, 0xF2, 0xD3, 0x220, 0x23A, 0xE5, 0x2C0-0x2C5 force color mode 4

Magic Numbers Reference:
  - 0x1a8: MonStats record size (424 bytes)
  - 0xa78: MonStats table offset in DataTables
  - 0xa80: MonStats table count offset
  - 0xC: Portal unit type
  - 0x275D: String ID for cold immune
  - 0x275E: String ID for fire immune
  - 0x1506: Special skill ID (no immunity display)
  - 0xF9B (3995): Newline/separator string ID

Flag Bits (MonStats offset 0xD):
  - Bit at gdwBitMasks[1] (0x4): If set, skip detailed tooltip
  - Bit at gdwBitMasks[7] (0x1C): Must be set for detailed tooltip

Color Modes (pcStack_1424):
  - 0: Normal monster (white)
  - 1: Portal/waypoint (blue)
  - 3: Champion monster (blue)
  - 4: Boss/unique monster (gold)

functions.name: RenderUnitNameOverlay
functions.comment:
Renders unit name overlay on screen for the specified unit.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if viewport mode is 3 (cinematic) or unit is null
2. For tile units (type 5), check distance threshold (>100) and exit if too far
3. Calculate screen position based on automap mode or isometric projection
4. Switch on unit type to render appropriate name display:
   - Type 0 (Player): Render player name with dialog control value
   - Type 1 (Monster): Handle special monsters (0x1A1/0x1A2 mercenary types), show skill info
   - Type 2 (Object): Render object name with quest/shrine info and network player names
   - Type 4 (Item): Build item tooltip for UI display
   - Type 5 (Tile): Render waypoint/tile name from level data

Parameters:
  pUnit - UnitAny* pointer to unit whose name to render

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
- Viewport mode 3 skips all rendering (cinematic mode)
- Monster types 0x1A1/0x1A2 are mercenary hirelings requiring skill data lookup
- Monster type 0x164 is a special interactive object
- Object flags at offset 0x167 determine rendering mode (0x04=quest, 0x40=shrine, 0x80=portal)
- Network sessions append player name in parentheses for objects
- Tile type 8 requires quest system initialization check

Magic Numbers:
- 0x1A1, 0x1A2: Mercenary monster class IDs
- 0x164: Barricade/interactive object monster ID
- 0x48: Y-offset for name positioning above unit
- 0x10: Additional Y-offset for screen projection
- 0xC7 (199): Max characters for tile name string

Structure Offsets:
- pUnit+0x00: Unit type (0=player, 1=monster, 2=object, 4=item, 5=tile)
- pUnit+0x04: Unit class ID / subtype
- pUnit+0x0C: Owner GUID
- pUnit+0x14: Unit data pointer
- pUnit+0xC4: Unit flags (bit 9 = special display mode)

functions.name: CalculatePartyMemberNameDisplayPosition
functions.comment:
Calculates and updates the screen position for displaying a party member's name.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if viewport mode is 3 (automap), no game context, or no roster list
2. Search roster list for player entry (type=7) matching current game's party ID
3. Early exit if entry has non-zero status at offset 0x20 or unit ID is invalid (-1)
4. Find the roster entry matching the unit ID and verify it's an active player (type=1)
5. Look up the unit in the hash table using the unit ID masked with 0x7F
6. Validate unit type is 1 (player), abort if mismatch
7. Check if using perspective mode (Ordinal_10037):
   - If NOT perspective (mode 0): Use direct unit position via Ordinal_10641/10057
   - If perspective mode: Convert 3D coordinates via Ordinal_10321/10607/10043/10046
8. Apply viewport offset adjustment based on g_dwViewportMode (1=left panel, 2=right panel)
9. Store final position in g_dwUnitNameDisplayState (X) and g_dwUnitNameCacheIndex (Y)
10. Call UpdateUnitNameDisplay(1) to render the name

Parameters:
None (uses globals)

Returns:
void - Updates g_dwUnitNameDisplayState and g_dwUnitNameCacheIndex globals

Special Cases:
- Returns immediately if viewport mode is 3 (automap view)
- Returns immediately if no game context or roster list exists
- Returns immediately if unit ID is 0xFFFFFFFF (invalid)
- Calls CleanupAndAbort if unit type validation fails (defensive check)

Magic Numbers:
- 7: Player unit type in roster entry
- 0x7F: Hash table mask for 128-bucket unit lookup
- 0x30: Offset to next roster entry pointer
- 0x24: Offset to roster entry data section
- 0xE4: Offset to next unit in hash chain
- 0x10: Y-axis offset added to final position
- 8: Y-axis viewport center adjustment

Viewport Mode Values:
- 0: Normal centered view
- 1: Left panel open (shift X negative by screen_width/4)
- 2: Right panel open (shift X positive by screen_width/4)
- 3: Automap view (function exits early)

functions.name: RenderPassiveSkillStateIcons
functions.comment:
Renders passive skill state icons on the game UI.

Iterates through the passive skill state table and renders icons for each
active skill effect. Icons are displayed in a row near the top-right of
the screen, with position adjusted based on game state (normal/expansion).

Algorithm:
1. Validate game context: level, game context, room, and state flag
2. Calculate initial icon X/Y position from screen dimensions
3. Adjust Y position if game state is expansion mode (state == 2)
4. Loop through passive skill state entries from sgptDataTables
5. For each skill entry:
   a. Get skill ID from state table (offset 0x16c)
   b. Check if unit has skill (Ordinal_10706)
   c. Verify skill is castable (Ordinal_10429)
   d. Get skill descriptor record and validate
   e. Check skill page and icon index bounds
   f. Get skill level via Ordinal_10550
   g. Render icon if level is 1-3 via FUN_6fb0f070
   h. Decrement X position by icon spacing for next icon

Parameters: None (uses global state)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- Early exit if g_pCurrentLevel is null
- Early exit if g_pGameContext is null
- Early exit if unit has no room
- Early exit if g_bSkillStateIconsEnabled is zero
- Game state 2 uses different Y offset (expansion UI)

Ordinal References:
- Ordinal_10706: D2Common.SKILLS_CheckUnitHasSkill - Checks if unit has skill
- Ordinal_10429: D2Common.SKILLS_CanCastSkill - Checks if skill can be cast
- Ordinal_10550: D2Common.SKILLS_GetSkillLevel - Gets current skill level

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x170: Passive skill state count offset in DataTables
- 0x16c: Passive skill state ID array offset in DataTables
- 0xbc0: Max skill desc page count in DataTables
- 0xbd4: Max state icon page in DataTables
- 0x0e: Skill page offset in SkillDescRecord
- 0x10: Skill flags offset in SkillDescRecord
- 0x18: State icon page offset in SkillDescRecord

functions.name: RenderPlayerTooltipOverlay
functions.comment:
Renders player unit tooltip overlay text if buffer has content.

Algorithm:
1. Check if g_wszTooltipBuffer (0x6fbd3f80) has text via Unicode::strlen
2. Get currently selected unit via GetSelectedUnitFromHash
3. Verify unit is a player (dwType == 1)
4. Check unit inventory data flags at offset 0x16:
   - Bit 0x8 set: Use text style 4 (corpse/dead state)
   - Bit 0x4 set: Use text style 3 (dying state)
   - Otherwise: Use text style 0 (normal)
5. Get current font property and add 0x27 offset for Y position

functions.name: RenderUnitStatSummaryOverlay
functions.comment:
Renders the unit stat summary overlay text when hovering over a player unit.

Algorithm:
1. Get the currently selected unit from the unit hash table
2. Verify the unit exists and is a player type (unit type == 1)
3. Get current font line height and add 0x27 (39) pixel vertical offset
4. Render the first text line (unit name buffer) at calculated Y position
5. If either description buffer or monster affix buffer contains text, add font height spacing

  g_wszMonsterAffixBuffer (0x6fbd3f80) - Check for monster affix text
