Each entry [i] = popcount(i) for i in 0..63

functions.name: PopulateItemStatRangesFromAttributes
functions.comment:
Populates an item stat range array by querying unit stats based on attribute table entries.

Algorithm:
1. Zero-initialize 42 DWORD stat range array (168 bytes) pointed to by ESI
2. Iterate through g_adwSoundAttributeTable entries (count from g_dwSoundAttributeTableCount)
3. For each attribute ID, call Ordinal_10190 (D2Common.GetStatValue) to retrieve stat value
4. Store result at specific offsets in the stat range array based on attribute type
5. For min/max damage pairs (0x15/0x16), fall back to alternate stats (0x17/0x18) if zero
6. For stat 0x3B, also fetch stat 0x146 via Ordinal_10550
7. Set validity flags to 1 for each stat pair where both min and max are positive

Parameters:
  pUnit (stack) - Unit pointer passed through to Ordinal_10550 for stat 0x146 lookup
  IMPLICIT EBX - Unit pointer for Ordinal_10190 stat lookups
  IMPLICIT ESI - Pointer to 42-DWORD stat range output array

Returns:
  void - Results stored in array pointed to by ESI

Stat Attribute Mapping (switch cases):
  0x11 -> offset 0x1C (array[7])   - Secondary max damage
  0x12 -> offset 0x18 (array[6])   - Secondary min damage
  0x15 -> offset 0x00 (array[0])   - Primary min damage (fallback: 0x17)
  0x16 -> offset 0x04 (array[1])   - Primary max damage (fallback: 0x18)
  0x30 -> offset 0x60 (array[24])  - Magic min damage
  0x31 -> offset 0x64 (array[25])  - Magic max damage
  0x32 -> offset 0x48 (array[18])  - Fire min damage
  0x33 -> offset 0x4C (array[19])  - Fire max damage
  0x34 -> offset 0x90 (array[36])  - Poison min damage
  0x35 -> offset 0x94 (array[37])  - Poison max damage
  0x36 -> offset 0x30 (array[12])  - Cold min damage
  0x37 -> offset 0x34 (array[13])  - Cold max damage
  0x39 -> offset 0x78 (array[30])  - Lightning min damage
  0x3A -> offset 0x7C (array[31])  - Lightning max damage
  0x3B -> offset 0x80 (array[32])  - Lightning extra + 0x146 at array[33]

Validity Flags (set to 1 if both min > 0 and max > 0):
  array[4]  - Primary damage valid
  array[10] - Secondary damage valid
  array[16] - Cold damage valid
  array[22] - Fire damage valid
  array[28] - Magic damage valid
  array[34] - Lightning damage valid
  array[40] - Poison damage valid

Called by: BuildItemDescriptionText

functions.comment:
Processes stat property IDs to determine if description text should be displayed
and formats range values for item stat tooltips.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 256-character Unicode buffer for formatted output
2. Switch on stat property ID to handle each stat type
3. For range stats, compare min/max values and format appropriately
4. Return 0 if no text should be displayed, 1 if formatted successfully
5. Direct field returns for simple flag checks (0x11, 0x31, 0x33, etc.)

  1 - Text was formatted and appended to output buffer
  Field value - For direct field return cases (0x11, 0x18, 0x31, 0x33, 0x35, 0x37, 0x3a/0x3b)

Stat Property ID Mapping:
  0x11 (17) - Return field at offset 0x28 directly
  0x12 (18) - Duration/charges text with special formatting
  0x15-0x17 (21-23) - Enhanced damage min/max range
  0x18 (24) - Enhanced damage flag check
  0x30 (48) - Lightning damage range (offsets 0x60/0x64)
  0x31 (49) - Lightning damage flag (offset 0x70)
  0x32 (50) - Fire damage range (offsets 0x48/0x4C)
  0x33 (51) - Fire damage flag (offset 0x58)
  0x34 (52) - Cold damage range (offsets 0x90/0x94)
  0x35 (53) - Cold damage flag (offset 0xA0)
  0x36 (54) - Poison damage range (offsets 0x30/0x34)
  0x37 (55) - Poison damage flag (offset 0x40)
  0x39 (57) - Magic/calculated damage with divisor normalization
  0x3a-0x3b (58-59) - Magic damage flag (offset 0x88)

Magic Numbers:
  0x100 (256) - Unicode buffer size for sprintf output
  0x80 (128) - Rounding constant for fixed-point arithmetic
  0x19 (25) - Divisor for damage calculation scaling
  0x0A (10) - Buffer size for duration string formatting

Structure Layout (StatRangeInfo* at in_EAX):
  Offset | Size | Field                    | Description
  -------|------|--------------------------|----------------------------

functions.name: BuildSocketStatDescription
functions.comment:
Builds the socket stat description text for item tooltips.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 256-element Unicode buffer for description
2. Fetch localized strings using D2Lang.GetLocalizedString (Ordinal_10004):
   - String 0xFA2 (4002): Socket label prefix
   - String 0xF9E (3998): Socket separator
   - String 0xF9B (3995): Socket count format
   - String 0xFA1 (4001): Socket label suffix
3. Initialize 20-element Unicode buffer for integer formatting
4. Format integer value using "%i" format string
5. Convert formatted integer to Unicode
6. Concatenate all components in order to build socket stat text
7. Fetch additional localized string 0xDE2 (3554)
8. Concatenate final components to destination buffer

Parameters:
- pDestBuffer (Stack[0x4]): Pointer to destination Unicode buffer for result

Returns:
- void (result written to pDestBuffer)

Called By:
- BuildItemDescriptionText: When item has sockets (stat 0x39) and not skill-related (stat 0x7A)

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10004 = D2Lang.GetLocalizedString: Fetches localized string by ID (ECX = string ID)

String IDs Used:
- 0xFA2 (4002): Socket prefix text
- 0xF9E (3998): Socket separator
- 0xF9B (3995): Socket count display
- 0xFA1 (4001): Socket suffix text
- 0xDE2 (3554): Additional socket text

Phantom Variables:
- unaff_ESI, unaff_EDI: Decompiler artifacts for register preservation, not actual source variables

functions.name: FormatResistanceStatDescription
functions.signature: void FormatResistanceStatDescription(int * pUnit, int nUnused, int * pStatDisplayEntry)
functions.comment:
Formats resistance stat descriptions for item tooltips.

Iterates over the stat display table searching for entries matching the item's
base stat type. For matching entries, retrieves the stat value (stat ID 0x47)
and formats it with appropriate sign prefix (+/-) for display.

Algorithm:
  1. Initialize two Unicode buffers (128 chars each) for positive/negative text
  2. Load three string table entries for formatting templates
  3. Get the item's base stat type via Ordinal_10075
  4. Iterate through g_dwStatDisplayTableCount entries in stat display table
  5. For each matching stat type:
     a. Clear format buffers
     b. Get stat value 0x47 (resistance percentage)
     c. Apply bit shift for stat types 6-11 (8-bit packed values)
     d. Load positive or negative string based on value sign
     e. Format numeric value using "%i" format string
     f. Build final string: prefix + value + suffix
  6. Advance to next table entry (+16 bytes)

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to unit/item data structure
  nUnused - Unused parameter (always 0 in observed calls)
  pStatDisplayEntry - Pointer into stat display table (g_adwData_6fba7934)
  IMPLICIT unaff_EBX - Destination Unicode string buffer (char*)
  IMPLICIT unaff_EDI - Source format string buffer (char*)

Returns:
  void - Output is written to implicit string buffer registers (EBX/EDI)

Stat Display Table Entry Structure (16 bytes):
  Offset | Size | Field          | Description
  -------|------|----------------|-----------------------------
  0x00   | 4    | nStatTypeId    | Stat type to match
  0x04   | 4    | nDisplayType   | 1=percentage, 2=range format
  0x08   | 2    | wPosStringId   | String ID for positive values
  0x0A   | 2    | wNegStringId   | String ID for negative values
  0x0C   | 4    | dwReserved     | Unused/padding

Stat Type Bit Shifting:
  Types 6,7   - Shift right 8 bits (fire/cold resist)
  Types 8,9   - Shift right 8 bits (lightning/poison resist)  
  Types 10,11 - Shift right 8 bits (magic/physical resist)

Ordinal Calls:
  Ordinal_10004 - D2Lang::GetLocaleString - Retrieves localized string by ID
  Ordinal_10075 - D2Common::GetItemStatIdentifier - Gets item base stat type ID
  Ordinal_10550 - D2Common::GetUnitStatValue - Gets stat value for unit

Magic Numbers:
  0x47 (71) - Stat ID for resistance percentage value
  0x80 (128) - Unicode buffer character count
  0x10 (16) - Stat display table entry stride
  0x141 (321) - Error code: invalid display type
  0x13d (317) - Error code: format type mismatch

functions.name: ValidateHirelingDescriptionStat
functions.signature: uint ValidateHirelingDescriptionStat(int * pUnit, uint dwSkillContext, int nExpectedIndex, int nExpectedStat, byte * pHirelingDescRecord, uint * pfIsExactMatch)
functions.comment:
Validates that a hireling's scaled stat matches an expected value.

Iterates backwards through all hireling description records to find entries
with matching hireling IDs, then verifies the calculated stat matches the
expected value for each match.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if hireling description record has no ID (offset 0x3E == 0)
2. Get hireling description count from sgptDataTables at offset 0xBD4
3. Loop backwards through all hireling description records (size 0x144 each)
4. For each record with matching hireling ID at offset 0x3E:
   a. Set exact match flag if current index equals nExpectedIndex
   b. Call Ordinal_10190 to update skill context
   c. Calculate scaled stat via CalculateHirelingScaledStat
   d. If calculated stat != nExpectedStat, return FALSE
5. Return TRUE if all matching records validated or no matches found

Parameters:
  pUnit - Unit pointer passed to CalculateHirelingScaledStat for stat scaling
  dwSkillContext - Skill context value passed to Ordinal_10190
  nExpectedIndex - Expected hireling index for exact match flag comparison
  nExpectedStat - Expected stat value to validate against calculated stat
  pHirelingDescRecord - Pointer to hireling description record being validated
  pfIsExactMatch - Output flag set to 1 if current index matches nExpectedIndex

Returns:
  1 (TRUE) - All hireling records with matching ID have valid stats
  0 (FALSE) - Input record has no ID, table lookup failed, or stat mismatch

Structure Layout (HirelingDesc record, size 0x144):
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  0x3E    2     wHirelingId   Hireling type identifier

Data Tables (sgptDataTables offsets):
  Offset  Size  Field              Description
  0xBCC   4     pHirelingDescTable Pointer to hireling description array
  0xBD4   4     nHirelingDescCount Number of hireling description records

Magic Numbers:
  0x144 - Size of each hireling description record (324 bytes)
  0x3E  - Offset to hireling ID field within record

functions.name: FormatHirelingStatDescription
functions.signature: int FormatHirelingStatDescription(int * pUnit, dword dwStatContext, dword dwStatParam)
functions.comment:
Formats a hireling (mercenary) stat description string for display in item tooltips.

Uses a 28-case switch statement to handle different stat description types, building
Unicode strings with appropriate formatting based on the stat type and display mode.

Algorithm:
1. Validate hireling index (in_EAX) against sgptDataTables bounds
2. Get hireling description record from table at offset 0xBCC (record size 0x144)
3. Call CalculateHirelingScaledStat to compute the stat value
4. Call ValidateHirelingDescriptionStat to verify stat consistency
5. Extract description type (offset 0x36/0x40) and display mode (offset 0x37/0x41)
6. Dispatch to appropriate case handler based on description type (1-28)
7. Build formatted Unicode string using strcpy/strcat operations
8. Handle suffix string index (offset 0x3C/0x46) for certain stat types

Parameters:
  pUnit - Pointer to unit structure for stat calculation context
  dwStatContext - Stat context value passed to validation functions  
  dwStatParam - Additional stat parameter for certain description types
  IMPLICIT in_EAX - Hireling index into HirelingDesc table

Returns:
  1 - Successfully formatted description string (output in ESI register)
  0 - Invalid hireling index, validation failure, or unsupported stat type

Description Type Switch Cases:
  1,6,12 - Basic stat with optional positive modifier prefix
  2,7 - Stat with value suffix
  3,9 - Stat with conditional display
  4,8 - Negative stat formatting (inverts value)
  5,10 - Percentage stat formatting
  11 (0xB) - Duration stat (converts to seconds, formats as X.X sec)
  13 (0xD) - Level-based stat with GetLevelDataRecord lookup
  14 (0xE) - Skill level stat with skill data lookup
  15 (0xF) - Monster stat with sound index lookup
  16 (0x10) - Monster name stat
  17-18 (0x11-0x12) - Level difficulty stat with Ordinal_11113
  19 (0x13) - Direct value formatting
  20-21 (0x14-0x15) - Negated stat value
  22 (0x16) - Element type stat with GetElemTypeRecord
  23 (0x17) - Skill stat with GetSkillDataFromId
  24 (0x18) - Compound stat (high/low byte split)
  25-26 (0x19-0x1A) - Signed stat formatting
  27 (0x1B) - Aura stat with Ordinal_10253 lookup
  28 (0x1C) - Monster type stat with GetMonsterDataFromId

Data Tables (sgptDataTables offsets):
  0xBA0 - Monster count limit
  0xBCC - pHirelingDescTable (pointer to hireling description array)
  0xBD4 - nHirelingDescCount (number of records)
  0xC6C - Stat bit shift value
  0xC70 - Stat bit mask value

HirelingDesc Record Layout (size 0x144 = 324 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field              Description
  0x18    1     bStatShift         Bit shift for stat calculation
  0x36    1     bDescType          Description type (primary)
  0x37    1     bDisplayMode       Display mode (1=prefix, 2=suffix)
  0x38    2     wPosStringIndex    String table index for positive values
  0x3A    2     wNegStringIndex    String table index for negative values
  0x3C    2     wSuffixStringIndex String table index for suffix
  0x3E    2     wHirelingId        Hireling type identifier
  0x40    1     bDescType2         Description type (secondary/scaled)
  0x41    1     bDisplayMode2      Display mode (secondary)
  0x42    2     wPosStringIndex2   Positive string (secondary)
  0x44    2     wNegStringIndex2   Negative string (secondary)
  0x46    2     wSuffixIndex2      Suffix string (secondary)
  0x52    2     wLevelNameIndex    Level name string index
  0x54    6     awSkillStrings[3]  Skill string indices
  0x5A    2     wSkillSuffixIndex  Skill suffix string index

Magic Numbers:
  0x144 - HirelingDesc record size (324 bytes)
  0x9C4 - Duration base value (2500, for seconds calculation)
  0x1E - Duration threshold (30 seconds)
  0x19 - Seconds divisor (25)
  0x1506 - Special string index for alternate suffix handling

functions.name: BuildSkillBonusDescription
functions.signature: void BuildSkillBonusDescription(int nUnitId, ushort * pOutputBuffer, int nDescriptionType)
functions.comment:
BuildSkillBonusDescription - Formats skill bonus text for item/hireling tooltips

Algorithm:
1. Initialize two 128-element Unicode buffers for string building
2. Load localized format strings from string table (IDs 0xf9e, 0xfa2, 0xfa3, 0xf9b)
3. Call Ordinal_10341 to retrieve skill bonus data for the unit
4. For each skill bonus entry:
   a. Extract skill ID and bonus value from results array
   b. Look up skill name from data tables using skill ID
   c. Format bonus value as numeric string using "%i" format
   d. Build description string: [prefix] [value] [skill name]
   e. If nDescriptionType == 0x6b (107): append class-specific skill info
      via Ordinal_10253 lookup against PlayerClass table
5. Concatenate all formatted entries to output buffer

Parameters:
  nUnitId - Unit identifier for skill bonus lookup
  pOutputBuffer - Destination Unicode string buffer for formatted text
  nDescriptionType - Description format type (0x6b triggers class skill append)

Returns:
  void - Output written directly to pOutputBuffer

Data Table Offsets (via sgptDataTables):
  0xb8c - Skill description string table pointer
  0xb94 - Skill description table row count
  0xb98 - Skill data table base pointer  
  0xba0 - Skill table row count
  0xbc4 - PlayerClass table base pointer
  0xbc8 - PlayerClass table row count

Magic Numbers:
  0x6b (107) - Description type triggering class skill name append
  0x80 (128) - Buffer size for Unicode string arrays
  0xf9e, 0xfa2, 0xfa3, 0xf9b - Localized string table indices
  0x23c (572) - Skill record stride size
  0xc4 (196) - PlayerClass record stride size
  0x194 - Offset to skill string index within skill record
  0x5a - Offset to class name string index within PlayerClass record

functions.name: BuildSetItemBonusDescription
functions.comment:
Builds set item bonus description text for tooltip display.

Checks if the unit is an item (type 5) with valid SetItems.txt data,
then iterates through 6 possible stat slot IDs looking for matching
set bonus properties. When a match is found, delegates to
BuildItemDescriptionText to format the stat bonus text.

Algorithm:
1. Get unit type via Ordinal_10911, verify it's an item (type == 5)
2. Get SetItems.txt row index via Ordinal_10075, validate range
3. Calculate SetItemsTxt record pointer: base + (index * 0x1b8)
4. Loop through g_dwItemStatSlotIds[0..5] array
5. For each slot ID, get stat item via Ordinal_10429
6. Get stat value via Ordinal_10190 with stat ID 0x47 (71)
7. Compare against SetItemsTxt record stat at offset +0x2c
8. On match, call BuildItemDescriptionText with matched slot ID

Parameters:
  pwOutputBuffer - Output buffer for formatted Unicode description text
  dwBufferSize   - Size of output buffer in characters
  IMPLICIT EAX   - pUnit: Pointer to unit being described
  IMPLICIT EBX   - pItem: Pointer to item for stat lookup

Returns:
  void - Output written to pwOutputBuffer

Magic Numbers:
  0x5   - Unit type: Item (UNIT_TYPE_ITEM)
  0x1b8 - SetItemsTxt record stride (440 bytes)
  0xc18 - sgptDataTables offset to SetItemsTxt array base
  0xc1c - sgptDataTables offset to SetItemsTxt record count
  0x47  - Stat ID 71 for set bonus property lookup
  0x2c  - SetItemsTxt offset to stat comparison field (short)
  6     - Maximum stat slot IDs to iterate

Structure Layout (SetItemsTxt at iVar1):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
  0x2c    2     wStatProperty   short   Set bonus stat property ID

functions.name: BuildPartialSetItemBonusText
functions.comment:
Builds partial or full set item bonus description text for tooltip display.

Checks if the unit is an item (unit type 4) of set quality (item type 5)
and retrieves set item data to determine bonus display mode. Supports
two modes based on SetItemsTxt.bBonusMode field at offset +0x87:
  Mode 1 (Partial): Uses bitmask to show bonuses for equipped set pieces
  Mode 2 (Full): Uses lookup table to show accumulated set bonuses

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer is non-null and unit type == 4 (item)
2. Get item quality via Ordinal_10911, verify == 5 (set item)
3. Get SetItemsTxt record pointer via Ordinal_10346
4. Read bBonusMode byte at SetItemsTxt+0x87
5. If mode == 1 (partial bonus):
   a. Get equipped set piece bitmask via Ordinal_10941(pUnit, pItem, 0)
   b. Get current item's set index via Ordinal_10189
   c. Loop through 6 stat slots (0-5), skip current item's index
   d. For each slot with bit set in mask, call BuildItemDescriptionText
6. If mode == 2 (full bonus):
   a. Get set bonus index via Ordinal_10941(pUnit, pItem, 1)
   b. Look up stat count from g_adwSetBonusStatCounts[index]
   c. Loop through (count-1) stat slots
   d. Call BuildItemDescriptionText for each slot

Parameters:
  pwOutputBuffer - Output buffer for formatted Unicode description text
  dwBufferSize   - Size of output buffer in bytes
  IMPLICIT EDI   - pItem: Pointer to set item unit being described
  IMPLICIT EAX   - pUnit: Pointer to player unit for context

Returns:
  void - Output written to pwOutputBuffer via BuildItemDescriptionText

Magic Numbers:
  0x4    - Unit type: Item (UNIT_TYPE_ITEM)
  0x5    - Item quality: Set item (ITEM_QUALITY_SET)
  0x87   - SetItemsTxt offset to bBonusMode byte
  0x01   - Partial set bonus mode (per-piece bonuses)
  0x02   - Full set bonus mode (accumulated bonuses)
  0x40   - Maximum valid set bonus index (64)
  6      - Maximum stat slot IDs to iterate

Global Data:
  g_dwItemStatSlotIds (0x6fb83b50) - Array of 6 stat slot IDs [0xA5-0xAA]
  g_adwSetBonusStatCounts (0x6fb87780) - Lookup table: index -> stat count

functions.name: FormatItemSkillBonusDescription
functions.comment:
Formats skill bonus descriptions for item tooltips.

This function generates formatted skill bonus text for display in item tooltips.
It handles two types of skill bonuses:
  - Single skill bonus (stat 0x14): Individual skill level increases
  - Class skill bonus (stat 0x4a): Bonuses to all skills of a class

Algorithm:
1. Initialize a 256-entry Unicode buffer for temporary string storage
2. Validate skill stat 0x35 is present on the item; abort if not
3. Retrieve skill info record using unit class ID via Ordinal_10994
4. Clear output buffer and check stat type:
   - If stat 0x14 (single skill): Use FormatSkillDescriptionLine
   - If stat 0x4a (class skill): Use FormatMultiLineSkillDescription
5. For each skill bonus type, format 4 description lines:
   - Type 2: Current level description
   - Type 1: Next level description (x2)
   - Type 0: Base level description
6. Each line is prefixed with separator strings from string tables
7. Append final separators and return

Parameters:
  nMaxLength (stack): Maximum length for formatted output (typically 0x200)
  IMPLICIT in_EAX: Pointer to unit/item with skill bonus stats
  IMPLICIT unaff_ESI: Output Unicode buffer for formatted description
  IMPLICIT unaff_EBP: Secondary string parameter for concatenation
  IMPLICIT unaff_EDI: Target buffer for string concatenation

Returns:
  void - Results written to implicit output buffers

Magic Numbers:
  0x35 - Skill stat identifier (general skill presence check)
  0x14 - Single skill bonus stat ID
  0x4a - Class skill bonus stat ID
  0xf0 - Offset in skill info record to skill text pointer
  0x100 - Size of temporary buffer (256 Unicode chars)
  0xf9e, 0xf9b - String table indices for separator text
  0x2b42, 0x2b41, 0x2b44, 0x2b43 - String table indices for skill descriptions

Error Codes:
  0x21a - Skill stat 0x35 not found on item
  0x21c - Failed to get skill info from Ordinal_10994
  0x223 - Failed to get skill text for single skill bonus
  0x245 - Failed to get skill text for class skill bonus

functions.comment:
Dumps comprehensive memory diagnostics to "D2Mem.txt" file for debugging memory allocations.

Algorithm:
1. Create file "D2Mem.txt" with GENERIC_WRITE access
2. Write header "D2 MEMORY CHECK" with separator line
3. Initialize exception frame for structured exception handling
4. Iterate through all memory heap allocations using SearchItemByHash
5. For each heap entry, allocate a 0x130-byte tracking node
6. Copy heap info (0x4A dwords = 0x128 bytes) into tracking node
7. Insert node into sorted doubly-linked list ordered by allocation size
8. Write per-heap statistics table: SIZE, BLOCKS, RESERVED, COMMITTED, MAX, REGIONS, FILENAME:LINE
9. Accumulate and write totals: NUM HEAPS, TOTAL MEMORY, TOTAL BLOCKS, etc.
10. Initialize second pass using ComputeHashIfSystemInitialized for allocation block walk
11. Iterate allocation blocks looking for debug marker pattern
12. Search for magic signature "DOLAFUCKTHISNOW " (ASCII debug marker)
13. Write matching tagged allocations with size and source location
14. Write final totals: TOTAL MEMORY, TOTAL ALLOC, TOTAL BLOCKS
15. Close file handle and unwind exception frame

Parameters:
    None

Returns:
    void

Special Cases:
    - Allocation failure during node creation results in NULL node
    - Empty heap list skips iteration entirely
    - Blocks smaller than 0x220 bytes are skipped in marker search

Magic Numbers Reference:
    0x40000000 - GENERIC_WRITE file access flag
    0x80 - FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL
    0x2 - CREATE_ALWAYS disposition
    0x128 (296) - Size of heap info structure
    0x130 (304) - Size of tracking node (296 + 8 byte list pointers)
    0x4A (74) - Number of dwords to copy (0x128/4)
    0x220 (544) - Minimum block size to search for debug marker
    0x12c (300) - Offset to allocation size in tracking node
    Debug marker pattern (16 bytes):
        0x4c4f4144 = "DOLA" (little-endian "ALOD")
        0x4655434b = "FUCK" 
        0x54484953 = "THIS"
        0x4e4f5720 = " NOW" (with leading space)

Structure Layout (Heap Tracking Node - 0x130 bytes):
    Offset  Size  Field              Description
    0x00    4     pNext              Next node pointer
    0x04    4     pPrev              Previous node pointer  
    0x08    296   heapInfo           Copied heap information
    0x10    N     szFilename         Source filename (embedded)
    0x114   4     dwLineNumber       Source line number
    0x118   4     dwTotalMemory      Total memory for this heap
    0x11c   4     dwSize             Allocation size
    0x120   4     dwMaxSize          Maximum allocation size
    0x124   4     dwRegionCount      Number of regions
    0x128   4     dwBlockCount       Number of blocks
    0x12c   4     dwAllocSize        Used for sorting

Error Handling:
    - Uses SEH (Structured Exception Handling) via exception frame
    - Allocation failures gracefully handled with NULL checks
    - File handle properly closed via CloseHandle before return

functions.name: InitializeGameViewportConfig
functions.comment:
Initialize game viewport configuration state by invoking Storm.dll function.

Algorithm:
1. Push three zero parameters (context flags, reserved, flags) onto stack
2. Call Ordinal_10034 (Storm.GetDisplayMode - retrieves display configuration)
3. Store AL register result (display mode byte) to global g_byViewportConfigState
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
None (void function)

Returns:
void - Updates g_byViewportConfigState with display mode configuration from Storm.dll

Special Cases:
Function always called before viewport rendering initialization (InitializeViewportRendering).
Result stored as single byte despite EAX return value (upper 3 bytes discarded).
Zero parameters to Storm.GetDisplayMode indicate query-only operation (no flags set).

Related Functions:
- InitializeViewportRendering() - Caller; uses this function to initialize display state first
- RenderPlayerStatisticsOverlay() - References g_byViewportConfigState indirectly via rendering logic

functions.name: RenderInventoryPanelBorders
functions.comment:
Renders the four corner border sprites for an inventory/skill tree panel.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize a sprite draw context structure (52 bytes) to zero
2. Store the sprite cell data pointer and set unused field to 0
3. Draw base corner sprites (frames 0-3) at the four corners:
   - Frame 0: Top-left (X offset -0x140, Y offset -0xE0)
   - Frame 1: Top-right (X offset -0x40, Y offset -0xE0)
   - Frame 2: Bottom-left (X offset -0x140, Y offset -0x30)
   - Frame 3: Bottom-right (X offset -0x40, Y offset -0x30)
4. Draw additional corner sprites based on sprite set index:
   - Calculate base frame as (nSpriteSetIndex * 4)
   - Draw frames nBase through nBase+3 at the same four positions

Parameters:
  pSpriteCellData - Pointer to sprite cell data (stored in context at offset 0x34)
  nSpriteSetIndex - Index multiplied by 4 to select sprite set frames

Returns:

  pnTempSecondary - Temporary storage pointer used by GetPlayerWeaponItems for secondary price

Returns:
  void - Results are written to output pointer parameters (pnPrimaryWeaponPrice, pnSecondaryWeaponPrice)

Notes:
- Uses CalculateItemSellPriceWrapper at 0x6fae26a0 as callback for price calculation
- Primary weapon slot is 4, secondary weapon slot is 5 in player inventory
- Temp pointers are zeroed after copying to prevent stale data on subsequent calls
- If no weapon equipped in a slot, corresponding price output will be 0

functions.name: GetPlayerWeaponItemSellPrices
functions.signature: int GetPlayerWeaponItemSellPrices(int * pPrimaryPrice, int * pSecondaryPrice, int nUnused1, int * pPrimaryValue2, int * pSecondaryValue2, int * pUnused2)
functions.comment:
GetPlayerWeaponItemSellPrices - Retrieves sell prices for player's equipped weapon items.

Thunk wrapper that invokes GetPlayerWeaponItems with CalculateItemSellPriceWrapper callback
to populate output parameters with primary and secondary weapon item sell price data.

Algorithm:
  1. Save EAX to stack for later use
  2. Load pUnused2 from stack param [ESP+0x14]
  3. Push param_10=0 (unused by callback)
  4. Push CalculateItemSellPriceWrapper (0x6fae26a0) as param_8 callback
  5. Push param_7=0 (unused)
  6. Load pSecondaryValue2 from [ESP+0x1c]
  7. Push param_9=0 (unused)
  8. Push pSecondaryPrice from EDX as param_6
  9. Load pPrimaryValue2 from [ESP+0x20]
  10. Push pUnused2 as param_5
  11. Load nUnused1 from [ESP+0x20]
  12. Push pSecondaryValue2 as param_4
  13. Push nUnused1 as param_3
  14. Push pPrimaryValue2 as param_2
  15. Call GetPlayerWeaponItems at 0x6fae24e0
  16. Return and clean 16 bytes from stack

Parameters:
  ECX pPrimaryPrice      - Output pointer for primary weapon sell price
  EDX pSecondaryPrice    - Output pointer for secondary weapon sell price
  [ESP+0x04] nUnused1    - Unused int parameter (passed through to callee)
  [ESP+0x08] pPrimaryValue2   - Output pointer for primary weapon value 2
  [ESP+0x0C] pSecondaryValue2 - Output pointer for secondary weapon value 2
  [ESP+0x10] pUnused2         - Unused output pointer (passed through)

Returns:
  int - Result from GetPlayerWeaponItems
        1 = Success, price data populated in output pointers
        0 = Failure, no valid weapon items found

Special Cases:
  - Zeros are passed for unused parameters (7, 9, 10)
  - Callback function handles actual price calculation

Calling Convention:
  __fastcall with RET 0x10 (cleans 16 bytes / 4 stack parameters)

functions.name: RenderHirelingPhysicalDamage
functions.signature: void RenderHirelingPhysicalDamage(int pContext, int pUnit, short * pnSkillId, int nMonsterLevel, int nXPos, int nYPos, int nColor)
functions.comment:
Calculates and renders the physical damage range for a hireling (mercenary).

Algorithm:
1. Validate pUnit and pnSkillId parameters are non-null
2. Extract skill ID from pnSkillId pointer
3. Calculate base min damage via Ordinal_10687 with skill and monster level
4. Calculate base max damage via Ordinal_10196 with skill and monster level
5. Compute hireling damage bonus from CalculateHirelingDamageBonus()
6. Get monster table level offset and add to total bonus
7. Set bonus flag to 3 if total bonus is non-zero
8. Apply Ordinal_10339 to get additional damage modifiers
9. Scale damage values via CalculateScaledDivision (base 100)
10. Accumulate skill-based damage via AccumulateSkillDamageFromStats
11. Combine min/max damage totals
12. Render formatted damage range via RenderFormattedNumberRange

Parameters:
  pContext      - int    - Game context/state pointer (passed via ECX __fastcall)
  pUnit         - int    - Unit/hireling pointer (passed via EDX __fastcall)
  pnSkillId     - short* - Pointer to skill ID value
  nMonsterLevel - int    - Monster/hireling level for damage scaling
  nXPos         - int    - X screen position for rendering
  nYPos         - int    - Y screen position for rendering
  nColor        - int    - Text color for rendering

Returns:
  void - Renders directly to screen

Calling Convention: __fastcall (ECX=pContext, EDX=pUnit, stack=remaining)

Callees:
  Ordinal_10687 @ 6fabc6c2 - Calculate min damage
  Ordinal_10196 @ 6fabc65c - Calculate max damage
  CalculateHirelingDamageBonus @ 6fae4b30 - Get hireling bonus
  GetMonsterTableLevelOffset @ 6fab2bc0 - Get level-based offset
  Ordinal_10339 @ 6fabcdca - Apply damage modifiers
  CalculateScaledDivision @ 6fab1a40 - Scale by 100
  AccumulateSkillDamageFromStats @ 6fae4960 - Add skill damage
  RenderFormattedNumberRange @ 6fae4080 - Render min-max range

Magic Numbers:
  0x1 - Damage calculation mode parameter
  0x3 - Bonus flag when bonus is active
  0x64 (100) - Scaling divisor for percentage calculations
  >> 8 - Extract integer portion from fixed-point (8-bit fractional)

functions.name: RenderSkillDamageWithBonuses
functions.signature: void RenderSkillDamageWithBonuses(void * pUnit, int bValidate, void * pSkillData, short * pnCalcId, int nSkillLevel, int nPosX, int nPosY)
functions.comment:
Calculates and renders skill damage values with attribute bonuses for UI display.

Algorithm:
1. Validate bValidate and pSkillData parameters are non-null
2. Get skill record from unit's skill data at offset 0x60 via Ordinal_11114
3. Extract skill ID from record (offset 0x4) or use -1 if null
4. Get skill description data via Ordinal_10994, read base damage percent at offset 0xFE
5. Check for skill synergy via Ordinal_10984 and apply bonus if applicable
6. Calculate base damage using GetSkillCalcValue with skill level
7. Apply strength bonus: damage += (strength * strBonus) / 100 via Ordinal_10571
8. Apply energy bonus: damage += (energy * energyBonus) / 100 via Ordinal_10765
9. Add flat bonuses from stats 0x19 (mindamage), 0x12 (maxdamage), 0x11 (secondary)
10. Determine color code (3 for special, 1 for normal, 0 for default)
11. Clamp minimum damage to -90 (0xFFFFFFA6)
12. Calculate final min/max values and render via RenderFormattedNumberRange

Parameters:
  pUnit (void*, ECX): Pointer to the unit whose skill damage to calculate
  bValidate (int, EDX): Boolean flag to enable validation checks
  pSkillData (void*, stack): Pointer to skill data structure
  pnCalcId (short*, stack): Pointer to skill calculation ID for lookup
  nSkillLevel (int, stack): Current skill level for damage calculation
  nPosX (int, stack): X position for rendering the damage text
  nPosY (int, stack): Y position for rendering the damage text

Returns:
  void - Renders damage range directly to screen

D2Common Ordinals Used:
  Ordinal_11114: GetSkillFromUnit - retrieves skill record from unit
  Ordinal_10994: GetSkillDescData - gets skill description table entry
  Ordinal_10984: GetSkillSynergyId - checks for synergy bonuses
  Ordinal_10706: CheckUnitState - validates unit state flag 0x65
  Ordinal_10007: GetUnitState - gets unit state value
  Ordinal_10687: GetSkillBonus - retrieves skill bonus value
  Ordinal_10196: SetSkillBonus - applies skill bonus
  Ordinal_10550: GetUnitStat - retrieves unit attribute (0=str, 2=energy, 0x11/0x12/0x19=damage)
  Ordinal_10571: GetStrengthDamageBonus - percentage bonus from strength
  Ordinal_10765: GetEnergyDamageBonus - percentage bonus from energy
  Ordinal_11083: IsSpecialRenderMode - checks for special color rendering
  Ordinal_10787: IsNormalRenderMode - checks for normal color rendering

Magic Numbers:
  0x60: Offset to skill data in unit structure
  0xFE: Offset to base damage percent in skill description
  0x65: Unit state flag for skill validation
  0x75: Skill bonus type identifier
  0x19 (25): Stat ID for minimum damage bonus
  0x12 (18): Stat ID for maximum damage bonus
  0x11 (17): Stat ID for secondary damage stat
  0xFFFFFFA6 (-90): Minimum damage floor value
  100: Divisor for percentage calculations

functions.name: RenderSkillElementalDamage
functions.signature: void RenderSkillElementalDamage(void * pUnit, int nSkillId, int nSkillLevel, int nDisplayMode, int nXPos, int nYPos, int nHeight)
functions.comment:
Renders elemental damage range for a skill in the UI tooltip/display.

Algorithm:
1. Validate skill ID and level are non-zero
2. Get skill data structure from unit offset 0x60
3. Retrieve skill data via Ordinal_10627 (D2Common.GetSkillData)
4. Validate skill data exists via Ordinal_11090 (D2Common.ValidateSkillData)
5. Get fire mastery percentage via Ordinal_10571 (D2Common.GetSkillFireMastery)
6. Calculate fire bonus: (base_damage * fire_mastery%) / 100
7. Get lightning mastery via Ordinal_10765 (D2Common.GetSkillLightningMastery)
8. Calculate lightning bonus: (energy_damage * lightning_mastery%) / 100
9. Retrieve elemental damage stats:
   - Stat 0x9F (159): Min elemental damage
   - Stat 0xA0 (160): Max elemental damage
   - Stat 0x19 (25): Cold damage bonus
   - Stat 0x12 (18): Min magic damage
   - Stat 0x11 (17): Max magic damage
10. Apply damage modifier floor (-90 minimum)
11. Scale damage by modifier percentage
12. Check for synergy bonus (stat 0x4E) via Ordinal_10706
13. Apply synergy via Ordinal_10017 if present
14. Scale min/max by 100 using CalculateScaledDivision
15. Accumulate elemental damage types via AccumulateElementalDamageStats
16. Compare min/max and use larger as max
17. Scale by 128 (0x80) for display precision
18. Calculate item display dimensions
19. Render formatted number range to screen

Parameters:
  pUnit (ECX): Pointer to UnitAny structure for the caster
  nSkillId (EDX): Skill identifier to get damage for
  nSkillLevel (Stack+0x04): Current skill level
  nDisplayMode (Stack+0x08): Display mode/type flag
  nXPos (Stack+0x0C): X coordinate for rendering
  nYPos (Stack+0x10): Y coordinate for rendering  
  nHeight (Stack+0x14): Height offset for text

Returns:
  void - Renders damage range directly to screen

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if nSkillId or nSkillLevel is 0
  - Returns early if unit has no skill data at offset 0x60
  - Returns early if skill data validation fails
  - Damage modifier clamped to minimum -90 (-0x5A)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x60 - Unit offset to pSkillList pointer
  0x9F (159) - STAT_ELEMENTAL_MIN_DAMAGE
  0xA0 (160) - STAT_ELEMENTAL_MAX_DAMAGE
  0x19 (25) - STAT_COLD_DAMAGE_BONUS
  0x12 (18) - STAT_MAGIC_MIN_DAMAGE
  0x11 (17) - STAT_MAGIC_MAX_DAMAGE
  0x4E (78) - STAT_SKILL_SYNERGY_BONUS
  0x51EB851F - Fixed-point division constant (100)
  0x80 (128) - Display scaling factor

functions.name: RenderSkillRadiusValue
functions.signature: void RenderSkillRadiusValue(UnitAny * pUnit, int nUnused, SkillDescriptor * pSkillDesc, int nUnused4, int nXPos, int nYPos, int nLineHeight)
functions.comment:
Renders a skill's radius value on screen by calculating the effective radius from skill descriptor data and unit stats.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input pointers (pUnit and pSkillDesc must be non-NULL)
2. Extract bShiftAmount from pSkillDesc->bShiftAmount (offset 0x1a4)
3. Extract dwBaseRadius from pSkillDesc->dwBaseRadius (offset 0x1a8)
4. Calculate shift as (bShiftAmount - 8) for fixed-point conversion
5. Compute scaledBaseValue = dwBaseRadius << shift
6. Get unit stat 137 (0x89) via D2Common.Ordinal_10518 (GetUnitStat)
7. Calculate final radiusValue = scaledBaseValue + unitStat
8. Pass radiusValue to RenderFormattedNumberRange for display

Parameters:
  pUnit (ECX) - UnitAny* pointer to unit structure, used to query stat 137
  nUnused (EDX) - Unused parameter, only checked for non-zero
  pSkillDesc (stack+0x04) - SkillDescriptor* containing radius data at offsets 0x1a4 and 0x1a8
  nUnused4 (stack+0x08) - Unused parameter
  nXPos (stack+0x0C) - X coordinate for text rendering
  nYPos (stack+0x10) - Y coordinate for text rendering  
  nLineHeight (stack+0x14) - Line height for text rendering

Returns:
  void - Renders text directly to screen, no return value

Structure Layout (SkillDescriptor):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type   Description
  0x1a4   1     bShiftAmount    byte   Shift amount for fixed-point calculation
  0x1a8   4     dwBaseRadius    uint   Base radius value before scaling

Magic Numbers:
  0x89 (137) - Unit stat ID for skill radius bonus (queried via D2Common.Ordinal_10518)
  0x08 - Fixed-point shift base subtracted from bShiftAmount

External Calls:
  Ordinal_10518 (D2Common) - GetUnitStat(pUnit, nStatId, nLayer) returns stat value
  RenderFormattedNumberRange - Formats and renders numeric value/range to screen

Special Cases:
  - Early exit if nUnused (EDX) is zero/NULL
  - Early exit if pSkillDesc is NULL

Calling Convention: __fastcall
  - ECX: pUnit (UnitAny*)
  - EDX: nUnused  
  - Stack: pSkillDesc, nUnused4, nXPos, nYPos, nLineHeight (RET 0x14 = 5 params)

functions.comment:

functions.name: RenderWeaponDamageWithBonuses
functions.signature: void RenderWeaponDamageWithBonuses(UnitAny * pUnit, int nItemPtr, short * pwItemCode, int nItemDataPtr, int nMinDmg, int nMaxDmg, int nDisplayMode)
functions.comment:
Renders weapon damage range with all applicable bonuses for item tooltip display.

Calculates total weapon damage by combining base damage, hireling bonuses, item stat
bonuses, socket/gem bonuses, and ethereal weapon damage bonuses.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if pUnit or nItemPtr is null
2. Get item code from pwItemCode[0] and quality byte at offset +0x1DC
3. Call GetItemQualityDisplayMode to determine tooltip color scheme
4. Retrieve base min damage via Ordinal_10687(pUnit, nItemCode, nMinDmg, 0)
5. Retrieve base max damage via Ordinal_10196(pUnit, nItemCode, nMaxDmg, 0)
6. Shift results right by 8 to normalize stat values
7. Call CalculateHirelingDamageBonus to add hireling contribution
8. Query damage stat values via Ordinal_10339(pUnit, &nMinCalc, &nMaxCalc, &nBonus)
9. Apply percentage scaling via CalculateScaledDivision with divisor 100
10. Accumulate base + bonus + hireling damage for min and max
11. Get enhanced damage percent via Ordinal_11081 from item data at offset +0x138
12. Check for socketed item at pUnit offset +0x60
13. If socket exists, check item type via Ordinal_10445
14. Process ethereal bonus if item has flag 0x2D via Ordinal_10601
15. Apply secondary item bonuses if different from primary
16. Call CalculateItemStatBonuses for final stat accumulation
17. Render formatted damage range via RenderFormattedNumberRange

Parameters:
pUnit (ECX) - UnitAny* pointer to unit (player/hireling) owning the weapon
nItemPtr (EDX) - int item instance pointer for damage stat lookup
pwItemCode - short* pointer to item type code at offset 0x00
nItemDataPtr - int pointer to item data structure (offset 0x138 has enhanced dmg)
nMinDmg - int base minimum weapon damage value
nMaxDmg - int base maximum weapon damage value
nDisplayMode - int tooltip display mode affecting color and format

Returns:
void - Renders damage range directly to screen via RenderFormattedNumberRange

Magic Numbers:
0x2D (45) - Ethereal stat identifier for bonus damage check
0x04 - Socket bonus type identifier for ethereal items
0x138 - Offset to enhanced damage percentage in item data structure
0x1DC - Offset to item quality byte in item structure
0x60 - Offset to socketed item pointer in unit structure
0x64 (100) - Percentage divisor for scaled damage calculations

Ordinal Reference (D2Common.dll):
Ordinal_10687 - GetMinDamageStat: Retrieves minimum damage stat
Ordinal_10196 - GetMaxDamageStat: Retrieves maximum damage stat
Ordinal_10339 - GetDamageStatValues: Queries damage stat array
Ordinal_11081 - GetEnhancedDamagePercent: Gets enhanced damage modifier
Ordinal_10627 - GetSocketedItem: Retrieves socketed item from slot
Ordinal_10445 - GetItemType: Returns item type identifier byte
Ordinal_10292 - GetItemStat: Gets specific stat value from item
Ordinal_10601 - HasItemFlag: Checks item flag bitmask for property
Ordinal_10955 - IsValidItem: Validates item pointer is usable
Ordinal_10833 - GetItemStatParam: Gets parameterized stat value
Ordinal_10977 - ApplyItemEffect: Applies item effect to damage calculation

functions.name: RenderWeaponDamageWithObjectBonus
functions.signature: void RenderWeaponDamageWithObjectBonus(UnitAny * pUnit, int nUnitId, int nMaxDamage, int nUnused, int nXPos, int nYPos, int nColor)
functions.comment:
Calculates and renders weapon damage range with object-based bonus modifiers.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit ID and max damage are non-zero, return early otherwise
2. Initialize local storage for min damage, max damage, and damage modifier
3. Calculate base weapon damage range via CalculateWeaponDamageRange
4. Look up object record from data tables using Ordinal_11151 (D2Common.ITEMS_GetItemTypeFromClass)
5. Validate object index is within bounds (0 <= index < count at offset 0xba0)
6. If valid object found, retrieve percentage bonus from offset 0x158 in object record
7. Apply percentage bonus to min damage: minDamage += (bonus * minDamage) / 100
8. Apply percentage bonus to max damage: maxDamage += (bonus * maxDamage) / 100
9. Apply additional item stat bonuses via CalculateItemStatBonuses
10. Render the final damage range with RenderFormattedNumberRange

Parameters:
  pUnit (ECX): Pointer to UnitAny structure for damage calculation context
  nUnitId (EDX): Unit ID used to look up object record in data tables
  nMaxDamage (Stack+0x4): Initial max damage value (reused as local storage)
  nUnused (Stack+0x8): Unused parameter - always ignored
  nXPos (Stack+0xC): X screen position for rendering output
  nYPos (Stack+0x10): Y screen position for rendering output  
  nColor (Stack+0x14): Text color value for damage display

Returns:
  void - Renders directly to screen, no return value

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x23c (572): Size of object record structure in bytes
  0x158 (344): Offset to damage bonus percentage field in object record
  0xba0 (2976): Offset to object count in sgptDataTables
  0xb98 (2968): Offset to object array pointer in sgptDataTables
  0xd40 (3392): Line number in SkillDesc.cpp for debug assertion
  0x51eb851f: Magic constant for fast integer division by 100

Special Cases:
  - Returns early if nUnitId is zero (no unit to look up)
  - Returns early if nMaxDamage is zero (no damage to display)
  - Object bonus is zero if object index is negative
  - Object bonus is zero if object index >= object count
  - Object bonus is zero if object record pointer is null

functions.name: RenderWeaponDamageWithKSuffix
functions.signature: void RenderWeaponDamageWithKSuffix(void * pItemContext, int nItemId, int nXPosition, int nYPosition, int nTextColor, int nShadowColor, int nFontId)
functions.comment:
Renders weapon damage range with K suffix for values >= 10000.

Formats and displays weapon damage statistics with automatic "K" suffix 
conversion for large numbers (thousands). Handles both base damage and 
bonus damage ranges, converting values like 10000-15000 to "10K-15K".

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if nItemId is 0 or nFontId is 0
2. Call CalculateWeaponDamageRange to get base min/max damage values
3. Call CalculateItemStatBonuses to get bonus min/max damage values
4. Call CalculateItemDisplayDimensions to get display width/height
5. If no display dimensions needed, call RenderFormattedNumberRange directly
6. Format base damage string:
   a. If min == max: format as "%d" (single value)
   b. If both < 10000: format as "%d-%d" (range without K)
   c. If min >= 10000: format as "%s%dK-%dK" (both with K suffix)
   d. If only max >= 10000: format as "%s%d-%dK" (mixed format)
7. Convert formatted ANSI string to Unicode (wchar_t buffer)
8. Format bonus damage string using same logic
9. Convert bonus string to Unicode
10. Call RenderCharacterStatsDisplay with both Unicode buffers

Parameters:
  pItemContext (ECX): Pointer to item context structure
  nItemId (EDX): Item identifier for damage lookup
  nXPosition: X coordinate for text rendering
  nYPosition: Y coordinate for text rendering  
  nTextColor: Color value for main text
  nShadowColor: Color value for text shadow
  nFontId: Font identifier for rendering

Returns:
  void - Renders directly to screen

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x2710 (10000): Threshold for K suffix application
  0x1f4 (500): Rounding offset for division by 1000 ((val + 500) / 1000)
  0x10624dd3: Magic multiplier for signed division by 1000
  0x20 (32): Unicode buffer size (32 wchar_t characters)
  0x80 (128): Flag passed to CalculateWeaponDamageRange

Format Strings:
  "%d" (0x6fb84fdc): Single damage value
  "%d-%d" (0x6fb84e44): Damage range without K suffix
  "%s%dK-%dK" (0x6fb8756c): Both values with K suffix
  "%s%d-%dK" (0x6fb87560): Min without K, max with K suffix

functions.name: RenderPercentageScaledSkillDamage
functions.signature: void RenderPercentageScaledSkillDamage(UnitAny * pUnit, int nSkillId, SkillDescriptor * pSkillDesc, int nUnused, int nTextColor, int nPosX, int nPosY)
functions.comment:
Renders a skill damage range scaled by a percentage modifier.

Retrieves the base min/max damage range for a skill, applies a percentage scale factor
from the SkillDescriptor (offset 0x1A5), and renders the result as a formatted number range.

Algorithm:
1. Validate nSkillId and pSkillDesc are non-zero
2. Read percentage scale factor (bScalePercent) from pSkillDesc+0x1A5 (byte, 0-255)
3. Call GetSkillDamageRange to get base nMinDamage/nMaxDamage values
4. Apply percentage scaling using fixed-point arithmetic:
   scaledValue = (value * bScalePercent + rounding) >> 7
   where rounding = (result >> 31) & 0x7F handles signed division rounding
5. Call CalculateItemDisplayDimensions to prepare display formatting
6. Call RenderFormattedNumberRange to display the scaled damage range

Parameters:
  pUnit        - UnitAny*       [ECX] Source unit for skill damage calculation
  nSkillId     - int            [EDX] Skill identifier (skill ID from skills.txt)
  pSkillDesc   - SkillDescriptor* [Stack+0x4] Skill descriptor containing scale percent
  nUnused      - int            [Stack+0x8] Unused parameter (always 0)
  nTextColor   - int            [Stack+0xC] Color index for rendered text
  nPosX        - int            [Stack+0x10] X coordinate for text rendering
  nPosY        - int            [Stack+0x14] Y coordinate for text rendering

Returns:
  void - Renders directly to screen, no return value

Notes:
- The scale percentage at offset 0x1A5 represents values 0-200% (0-255 mapped to 0-200)
- Fixed-point division by 128 (>>7) is used for percentage calculation
- The rounding formula handles signed arithmetic correctly
- This function is typically called during skill tooltip rendering

Callee Functions:
- GetSkillDamageRange (0x6fae7f10): Retrieves base damage range for skill
- CalculateItemDisplayDimensions (0x6fae3170): Prepares display layout
- RenderFormattedNumberRange (0x6fae4080): Renders min-max as formatted text

functions.name: RenderSkillPhysicalDamageRange
functions.signature: void RenderSkillPhysicalDamageRange(UnitAny * pUnit, int nValidationFlag, short * pSkillRecord, int nSkillContext, int nRenderParam1, int nRenderParam2, int nRenderParam3)
functions.comment:
Calculates and renders a skill's physical damage range in the UI.

Computes minimum and maximum physical damage values by combining base damage,
skill level bonuses, and percentage modifiers from item stats. The final damage
range is passed to RenderFormattedNumberRange for display formatting.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer and validation flag (early exit if null/zero)
2. Get item quality display mode from skill record offset 0x1DC
3. Calculate scaled item stats for the unit
4. Check if unit has weapon equipped via Ordinal_10058
5. Determine stat IDs based on weapon type:
   - Two-handed (type 2): Uses stat IDs 0x17 (min) and 0x18 (max)
   - One-handed/other: Uses stat IDs 0x15 (min) and 0x16 (max)
6. Clamp minimum damage to 1, maximum to at least 2
7. Ensure maximum >= minimum damage
8. Apply three damage contributions from skill record:
   - Offset 0x138: Primary physical min damage modifier
   - Offset 0x13C: Primary physical max damage modifier
   - Offset 0x140: Secondary damage modifier
9. Each contribution checks enhancement stat (0x149, 0x14B, 0x14A) and applies percentage bonus
10. Final damage values scaled by CalculateScaledDivision (x * multiplier / 100)
11. Render formatted damage range with display mode

Parameters:
  pUnit [ECX]: Pointer to UnitAny structure (player/monster unit)
  nValidationFlag [EDX]: Non-zero to enable processing, zero for early exit
  pSkillRecord [Stack+0x4]: Pointer to skill data record with damage offsets
  nSkillContext [Stack+0x8]: Skill context/level information
  nRenderParam1 [Stack+0xC]: First render parameter passed to RenderFormattedNumberRange
  nRenderParam2 [Stack+0x10]: Second render parameter passed to RenderFormattedNumberRange
  nRenderParam3 [Stack+0x14]: Third render parameter passed to RenderFormattedNumberRange

Returns:
  void - Renders damage range directly to UI

Magic Numbers:
  0x1DC - Skill record offset for quality byte
  0x1A5 - Skill record offset for skill level byte
  0x138 - Skill record offset for primary min damage modifier
  0x13C - Skill record offset for primary max damage modifier
  0x140 - Skill record offset for secondary damage modifier
  0x15/0x16 - One-handed weapon min/max damage stat IDs
  0x17/0x18 - Two-handed weapon min/max damage stat IDs
  0x149 - Primary min damage enhancement stat ID
  0x14A - Secondary damage enhancement stat ID
  0x14B - Primary max damage enhancement stat ID
  0x64 (100) - Percentage divisor for scaling

Ordinal Calls:
  Ordinal_10058 - D2Common.STATLIST_GetUnitStatBoolean: Check if unit has weapon equipped
  Ordinal_10443 - D2Common.INVENTORY_GetEquippedItem: Get equipped weapon item
  Ordinal_10550 - D2Common.STATLIST_GetUnitBaseStat: Get base stat value from unit
  Ordinal_11081 - D2Common.SKILLS_GetSkillDamage: Get skill damage modifier
